mlb.sp_quality.label: Starting-pitcher true-talent quality (SIERA/xFIP/Stuff+, projections)
mlb.sp_quality.mechanism: A starter's underlying ability to prevent runs per batter (K, BB, contact quality) determines run prevention for the innings he works.
mlb.sp_quality.rationale: Starter quality is the dominant single input for moneyline, total and F5 markets, but ERA is mostly noise over small samples; projections and skill-based estimators carry more signal. Subtle: the quantity that matters is quality per batter faced times batters faced, and quality against the specific lineup (platoon, pitch type), so season-level ERA/FIP should be a prior only.

mlb.sp_workload.label: Expected innings / batters faced / pitch count
mlb.sp_workload.mechanism: Batters faced is the volume multiplier for every pitcher counting stat (strikeouts, outs, hits, walks, earned runs) and sets how much bullpen exposure the game has.
mlb.sp_workload.rationale: Pitcher props are rate x opportunity; workload uncertainty is often a bigger source of variance than rate uncertainty. Subtle: realized pitch count and pull are not knowable pregame; only their distribution is. mlb.run_dist.label: Run-scoring distribution (inning-level, negative binomial) and correlations
mlb.run_dist.mechanism: Runs per team per game are overdispersed and inning-clustered, so threshold and total markets depend on distribution shape and the correlation between teams.
mlb.run_dist.rationale: Using Poisson underprices high-scoring tails and the probability of shutouts; markets with total/team-total/1st inning rungs need the whole distribution. Subtle: run correlation arises from shared park/weather, and teams' scoring has zero-inflated innings.
mlb.run_dist.measurement: Fit negative-binomial (or inning-level compound) models of team runs with park/weather/pitching covariates; estimate overdispersion and between-team correlation by season; simulate game by half-inning.

mlb.pa_sim.label: Plate-appearance outcome simulation (Markov / Monte Carlo game engine)
mlb.pa_sim.mechanism: Simulating each plate appearance given batter, pitcher, park and context propagates every input into all market outcomes consistently.
mlb.pa_sim.rationale: A PA-level engine yields joint distribution for hits, TB, HR, K, runs, F5, innings and totals from one set of assumptions, which is essential for correlated rungs and combos. Subtle: needs a log5/odds-ratio combination of batter and pitcher outcome rates, times-through-order and fatigue adjustments, and bullpen replacement logic.
mlb.pa_sim.measurement: Per-PA multinomial from batter rates x pitcher rates (odds-ratio method) x park x umpire x weather; update by TTO and pitch count; model hook rule; Monte Carlo ~10k games; calibrate against historical run and K distributions.

mlb.mention_text.mechanism: Whether a word is said during a broadcast depends on the announcers' habits and on events likely to trigger it.

mlb.roster_moves.rationale: Markets on trades/signings/call-ups depend on the calendar, team status (buyer/seller) and service-time rules. Subtle: reported intentions precede official moves; the contract resolves on official announcement.
mlb.roster_moves.measurement: Calendar of key dates; team-status features; historical frequency of the move type by team and window.

mlb.f3_split.label: First-three-innings run split and top-of-order exposure by lineup
mlb.f3_split.mechanism: The first three innings give every starter a full turn through the top of the order and are mostly pitcher-quality and lineup-top dependent.
mlb.f3_split.rationale: Early-innings markets depend on the starter at full strength and lineup order exposure; the bullpen is rarely involved. Subtle: only one pass through the order mostly, so TTO penalty is irrelevant but first-inning splits are noisy.
mlb.f3_split.measurement: Simulate innings 1-3 with confirmed lineup top-9 and starter first-TTO rates; compare with F5 rates.

mlb.tto.label: Times-through-the-order penalty and starter pull rates
mlb.tto.mechanism: Pitchers perform worse the more often hitters see them in a game, so outcome rates and the hook decision both depend on the batter's number of looks.
mlb.tto.rationale: TTO penalty is a known structural effect: K% falls and wOBA rises in the third trip; managers respond by pulling starters. Subtle: effect size differs by pitcher type (fewer pitch types, reliance on a primary pitch) and is confounded with pitch count and fatigue; for strikeouts it means lower expected K per BF late in the outing.
mlb.tto.measurement: Pitcher-specific K%, BB%, wOBA by TTO (1st/2nd/3rd) with shrinkage toward league TTO curve (multilevel model); combine with exit probability by TTO from manager hook model to get expected BF by TTO.

mlb.k_rates.label: Pitcher K%/whiff/CSW and opposing-lineup K% (platoon-split)
mlb.k_rates.mechanism: Strikeouts occur when a pitcher's swing-and-miss and called-strike ability meet hitters prone to striking out; lineup K% by handedness captures the hitter side.
mlb.k_rates.rationale: For strikeout markets the mean is BF x per-PA K probability; per-PA K% is a combination of pitcher K% and lineup K% (log5), adjusted for umpire, park and TTO. Subtle: lineup K% varies by pitcher handedness and by pitch type, and use of the confirmed lineup (including bench replacements) can shift lineup K% by several points; K% stabilises relatively quickly (~70 BF).
mlb.k_rates.measurement: Pitcher K%, CSW%, whiff% regressed (prior weight ~100 BF); lineup K% vs RHP/LHP for each batter in confirmed order weighted by expected PA; combine via odds-ratio/log5 with league K%, then add TTO, umpire and park adjustments.

mlb.sb_context.label: Stolen-base attempt rate, pitcher hold time, catcher pop time
mlb.sb_context.mechanism: Steal attempts depend on the runner, the pitcher's delivery time to the plate and the catcher's throw.
mlb.sb_context.rationale: SB props: P(reaches base) x attempt rate x success; rule changes (pickoff limits, bases) raised success rates. Subtle: attempts depend on game state (score, outs) and on the runner being on base after earlier PAs, so lineup slot and OBP matter.
mlb.sb_context.measurement: Runner attempts per opportunity (on first/second with open base) with shrink; opposing pitcher SB allowed rates and catcher caught-stealing%; P(on base) from OBP and PA count.

mlb.contact_dist.label: Hit/TB/RBI count distributions given PA count and lineup slot
mlb.contact_dist.mechanism: Count markets are sums over a small number of plate appearances, whose number depends on lineup slot and team offence.
mlb.contact_dist.rationale: Hits and total bases follow a compound distribution: PA count x per-PA outcome probabilities, so lineup slot and expected team runs scale volume. Subtle: PA count is random (extra-inning, blowouts, pinch hitters), thresholds at 1+ hit vs 2+ TB reflect different outcome tail shapes.
mlb.contact_dist.measurement: Distribution of PA by lineup slot and team total; per-PA outcome probabilities; simulate hits/TB/RBI counts and check against historical frequencies by slot.

mlb.pitch_type_whiff.label: Pitcher whiff/CSW by pitch type and batter handedness
mlb.pitch_type_whiff.mechanism: Each pitch type has its own swing-and-miss and called-strike rate against left- and right-handed hitters, which builds the pitcher's strikeout ability pitch by pitch.
mlb.pitch_type_whiff.rationale: Aggregate K% hides that a pitcher's strikeouts come mostly from one or two pitches (slider vs same-handed hitters, changeup vs opposite-handed). When the lineup has weakness to that pitch the effect compounds. Subtle: use whiff per swing and CSW per pitch by count (two-strike usage), because two-strike pitch choice differs from the overall mix.
mlb.pitch_type_whiff.measurement: Per pitch type x batter hand: usage, whiff/swing, CSW, putaway rate (K per two-strike pitch), with shrinkage toward the pitch-type league mean (prior ~150 pitches); recency weighting for pitch-shape changes.

mlb.lineup_whiff_by_pitch.label: Opposing lineup whiff/chase by pitch type and pitcher handedness (confirmed lineup)
mlb.lineup_whiff_by_pitch.mechanism: The confirmed batting order's swing-and-miss rates against the pitch types the starter will actually throw convert his arsenal into a specific expected strikeout rate.
mlb.lineup_whiff_by_pitch.rationale: Lineup K% in aggregate misses mechanism: a lineup that whiffs on sliders but not fastballs is strongly exposed to a slider-heavy pitcher. Subtle: only knowable after lineup confirmation; before that, project by regular starters and platoon. Weighted by expected PAs per slot.
mlb.lineup_whiff_by_pitch.measurement: For each batter in confirmed order, whiff% and chase% by pitch type vs pitcher hand (shrunk); expected lineup whiff = sum_slot PA_weight x sum_pitchtype usage x batter whiff on that type; compare with league average for same pitch mix.

mlb.lineup_k_platoon.label: Confirmed-lineup K% by handedness weighted by PA slot
mlb.lineup_k_platoon.mechanism: Strikeout risk of the actual nine hitters against this pitcher's handedness is a direct driver of the strikeouts per batter faced.
mlb.lineup_k_platoon.rationale: Team K% averages include players not in the lineup and ignore platoon; confirmed lineup K% vs the pitcher's hand can differ by several points. Subtle: before confirmation, use the probable lineup; bench-heavy rest days change K% quickly; switch hitters take opposite-hand splits.
mlb.lineup_k_platoon.measurement: Per batter K% vs RHP/LHP (regressed to prior by PA), weighted by expected PA share by lineup slot (top bat ~4.6 PA, bottom ~3.8 in typical games, scaled by team total); sum to lineup K%; compare to league baseline.

mlb.velo_trend.label: Velocity, spin and movement trend over recent starts (injury/fatigue flags)
mlb.velo_trend.mechanism: A drop in fastball velocity or spin, or changed extension, signals fatigue, mechanics change or injury and predicts worse outcomes and earlier exits.
mlb.velo_trend.rationale: Velocity trends precede performance changes and IL stints; a pitcher returning from injury often throws at lower velocity and has pitch limits. Subtle: weather (cold lowers velocity) and measurement differences by park matter; compare to the pitcher's own season distribution, not league.
mlb.velo_trend.measurement: Rolling mean fastball velocity by start vs season baseline (z-score), adjusted for temperature; spin rate, release point shift, extension; flag drops > a pre-specified z-score; combine with days of rest.

mlb.pitch_count_limit.label: Planned pitch cap: rehab/return, innings limits, season workload
mlb.pitch_count_limit.mechanism: Pitchers returning from injury, prospects and workload-managed starters have explicit pitch caps that truncate batters faced regardless of performance.
mlb.pitch_count_limit.rationale: A hard cap makes the outs/strikeouts distribution ceiling-bound; markets on thresholds above the cap are structurally unlikely. Subtle: caps are announced by managers/beat writers, sometimes only after the start, and previous start's pitch counts are the best public indicator of the ramp.
mlb.pitch_count_limit.measurement: Track pitch counts across last starts and layoff status; ramp pattern (e.g., 70, 85, 95); manager statements timestamped; flag first start after IL; estimate cap distribution.

mlb.sp_efficiency.label: Pitcher efficiency: pitches per PA, first-pitch strike, foul-ball and two-strike pitch counts
mlb.sp_efficiency.mechanism: Pitches per batter determine how many batters fit under a pitch cap, so efficiency scales expected batters faced.
mlb.sp_efficiency.rationale: A pitcher who throws 3.7 pitches per PA and has a 100-pitch cap faces about 27 batters; a 4.1 P/PA pitcher faces 24. Subtle: efficiency depends on the opponent's patience, strikeout rate (strikeouts cost more pitches) and park/umpire; high-K pitchers tend to have higher P/PA.
mlb.sp_efficiency.measurement: Pitcher P/PA overall and by outcome type, EWMA with shrinkage; adjust by opponent lineup P/PA (log5 style); BF_cap = pitch cap / expected P/PA.

mlb.opp_pitches_per_pa.label: Opposing lineup patience: pitches per PA, swing and foul rates
mlb.opp_pitches_per_pa.mechanism: Patient lineups run up pitch counts and lower batters faced, while aggressive lineups shorten outings only if they hit well.
mlb.opp_pitches_per_pa.rationale: Pitches per PA of the confirmed lineup moves expected outs under a pitch cap and walks; it interacts with the pitcher's efficiency and leash. Subtle: patience correlates with walks and strikeouts, so higher patience lowers BF but raises K per BF in some cases.
mlb.opp_pitches_per_pa.measurement: Lineup P/PA weighted by expected PA slot; swing% and foul% on two-strike counts; combine with the pitcher's P/PA to compute expected pitches per PA in this matchup.

mlb.catcher_framing.label: Catcher framing and receiving (extra called strikes)
mlb.catcher_framing.mechanism: A catcher who gets more borderline pitches called strikes raises the pitcher's strikeout and lowers walk rates.
mlb.catcher_framing.rationale: Framing differences between catchers add up to meaningful run values over a season; the effect enters K and BB markets and lineup/umpire interactions. Subtle: backup catchers on rest days change the environment, and the effect interacts with umpire zone and pitcher style.

mlb.umpire_k_bb_effect.label: Umpire-specific K%/BB% and run effect adjusted for pitcher/batter mix
mlb.umpire_k_bb_effect.mechanism: An umpire's tendencies convert directly into per-PA strikeout and walk probabilities for the game's participants.
mlb.umpire_k_bb_effect.rationale: UmpScorecards-style called-strike rates and zone size shift K% and BB% for both teams, with relevance to totals, pitcher K/BB props and first-inning markets. Subtle: effect sizes are smaller than park or pitcher effects, sample (games per umpire per season) is limited, and the interaction with pitch location profile matters (low-zone pitchers vs high-zone).
mlb.umpire_k_bb_effect.measurement: Umpire K% and BB% over expected given pitchers/batters (mixed model with umpire random effect), shrunk; zone area (called strikes above expected by location bin); apply to the pitchers' location distribution.

mlb.wind_vector_park.label: Wind vector relative to park orientation and roof state
mlb.wind_vector_park.mechanism: Wind blowing out or in along the field axis and the roof state change fly-ball carry and thus HR and total runs.
mlb.wind_vector_park.rationale: Raw wind direction (compass) is useless without park azimuth; in/out components and crosswinds differ by park geometry. Subtle: forecast error is larger for wind than temperature, and retractable roofs are decided close to first pitch.
mlb.wind_vector_park.measurement: Compute wind component = speed x cos(wind direction - park home-plate-to-centre bearing); HR/total multiplier from historical regression; roof status flag from team announcements.

mlb.air_density.label: Air density: temperature, humidity, pressure, altitude
mlb.air_density.mechanism: Lower air density reduces drag and increases ball carry, raising HR and scoring (Denver, hot days).
mlb.air_density.rationale: Altitude and temperature effects on carry are physical and large for Coors; humidity has a smaller effect. Subtle: the effect is nonlinear and already in park factors for altitude, so a game-level adjustment should be relative to the park's average conditions.
mlb.air_density.measurement: Air density from temperature, pressure, humidity at park; deviation from park norm; regression of HR/FB on density deviation.

mlb.roof_state.label: Retractable-roof / dome status and conditions
mlb.roof_state.mechanism: Roof status removes weather effects when closed and adds them when open, and decides rain-delay risk.
mlb.roof_state.rationale: Parks with retractable roofs have different run environments by state; markets on delays are near zero when closed. Subtle: the decision is typically made within hours of first pitch; historical roof states are inconsistently recorded.
mlb.roof_state.measurement: Roof flag from team/venue announcements; historical rule by forecast; interplay with weather features (zero out wind if closed).

mlb.forecast_precip_timing.label: Hourly precipitation probability and radar nowcast near first pitch
mlb.forecast_precip_timing.mechanism: Rain timing relative to first pitch determines whether a game starts on time, is delayed or postponed.
mlb.forecast_precip_timing.rationale: Delay markets resolve on whether a delay occurs; hourly probability is not enough, since a brief shower after the game does not matter. Subtle: probability of precipitation is not the same as delay likelihood, and decisions are made by the umpire crew/manager, with tarp use; calibrate with historical delays.
mlb.forecast_precip_timing.measurement: Hourly PoP and amount from first pitch -3h to +3h; radar nowcast; logistic model of delay on PoP, amount, park (roof) and season; calibrate on historical games.

mlb.game_completion_rules.label: Official-game thresholds, suspended and shortened game rules
mlb.game_completion_rules.mechanism: Rules for rain-shortened, suspended and postponed games decide whether markets resolve, void or use partial results.
mlb.game_completion_rules.rationale: A game shortened to five innings is official; a suspended game resumes later, which may change when and whether player props settle. Subtle: Kalshi wording (and its source) governs; the same game can be official for baseball and void for a market, so wording must be read per series.
mlb.game_completion_rules.measurement: Extract from m.rules_text: official-game threshold, treatment of suspended/postponed, tie in shortened game; encode resolve-rule flags per ticker.

mlb.ghost_runner_strategy.label: Extra-innings strategy: bunt rates, intentional walks, bullpen depth
mlb.ghost_runner_strategy.mechanism: With a runner on second to start extra innings, managers bunt and walk batters more, and bullpen depth and the home team's last at-bat structure matter.
mlb.ghost_runner_strategy.rationale: Extra-innings run expectancy is much higher than normal innings; knowing who wins depends on the home advantage of batting last. Subtle: usage of the top relievers in extras is limited, so depth matters.
mlb.ghost_runner_strategy.measurement: Run expectancy matrix for ghost-runner start; per-team bunt/IBB rates in extras; bullpen depth after nine innings.

mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.label: Pitcher HR vulnerability: HR/FB, barrels allowed, fly-ball rate by batter hand
mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.mechanism: Pitchers who allow fly balls and hard contact give up more home runs, and the hitter-pitcher combination determines the single-game probability.

m.quote_history.label: Kalshi bid/ask/last time series (pre-game through close)
m.quote_history.mechanism: The traded price aggregates every participant's information about this contract, including injury and lineup news that moves faster than public stats.
m.quote_history.rationale: A price series is both a feature (the late price is usually a strong prior that model inputs must add to, not replace) and the reference for any edge claim. Never use post-close values as pregame features.

Subtle: historical depth is only available if captured live, so the pregame view is whatever was snapshotted; reconstructing it from trades is approximate.
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Snapshot the book (top-N levels both sides) at fixed intervals before start; compute spread, depth within 2 cents of mid, imbalance. Compare model edge to half-spread plus fee to get executable edge.

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder (monotonicity, implied distribution)
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Rungs of a threshold ladder (e.g. 4+, 5+, 6+) must imply one coherent count distribution; deviations expose stale or mispriced rungs and reveal the market's implied mean and variance.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Ladders for the same player/game are strongly correlated, so edges on adjacent rungs are not independent bets and exposure must be sized per ladder. Subtle: because each rung is a survival probability P(X>=k), monotone non-increasing is a hard constraint, and fitting a Poisson/negative-binomial to the rungs gives an implied mean that can be compared to a model mean on a like-for-like basis.
m.ladder_structure.measurement: For each event/player collect all live rungs at one timestamp; check P(k) non-increasing; fit a discrete distribution (Poisson, negative binomial, or free-form isotonic) to mid prices; compare implied mean/variance and per-rung residual to the model; track which rungs the market lags when news arrives.

m.settlement_truth.label: Settled result, settlement value and timestamp
m.settlement_truth.mechanism: The settled value is the only ground truth for calibrating every other input and exposes rule-edge cases (overtime, voids, delayed games).
m.settlement_truth.rationale: Without exact settlement values, hit rates and calibration are computed against a proxy (box score) that may differ from Kalshi's source (official stats, correction windows). Subtle: stat corrections after the game (scoring changes, hit/error changes, assist reassignments) can flip a threshold, so the settlement timestamp and source matter.
m.settlement_truth.measurement: Join Kalshi settled result and settlement_value to the official box score by game id; flag disagreements and post-game scoring changes; keep settlement time minus game end time.

Official league box scores (see sport sources)

m.rules_text.label: Versioned rules_primary / settlement wording (OT, ties, postponement, void)
m.rules_text.mechanism: The settlement wording defines which events count (overtime, extra innings, shootout goals, delayed games, DNPs) and therefore changes the true probability of the same real-world sport.
m.rules_text.rationale: Identical-looking contracts can differ: whether overtime/extra innings counts, whether a player who does not play voids or settles at zero, how postponements and shortened games resolve, which official stat source governs. A model that ignores the wording mis-prices the tail. Subtle: wording changes between series/seasons, so it must be versioned per ticker rather than assumed.
m.rules_text.measurement: Pull rules_primary/rules_secondary per market and hash it; extract flags (counts_overtime, counts_shootout, void_if_dnp, postponement_rule, source) by pattern matching and manual review of each new template; join to every training row.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2: /markets, /markets/trades, /series/{series}/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks) /markets (rules_primary, rules_secondary, custom_strike)

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook / exchange reference prices with timestamps
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sharp sportsbook and exchange lines are a competing aggregation of information and the standard benchmark for fair probability.
m.external_lines.rationale: Using a de-vigged external line as a feature or benchmark is often a stronger baseline than any public-stats model, and disagreement with Kalshi flags either a stale Kalshi quote or a rule-wording difference. Subtle: books price different settlement terms (e.g. regulation vs including overtime, 'action' rules on postponements) so lines must be mapped to the Kalshi rule before comparison, and the timestamp of the line matters.
m.external_lines.measurement: Capture timestamped lines per book; de-vig (power or Shin method) per market; map to the Kalshi contract's rule (regulation vs full game, push handling); compute Kalshi minus consensus and closing-line value relative to the latest pregame consensus.
free_sources: The Odds API free tier (current lines only, limited quota)

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules in force
m.fees.mechanism: Fees reduce realized edge and depend on price level, so the break-even probability differs by rung and by maker/taker role.
m.fees.rationale: Because the fee is price-dependent, a fixed edge in cents is worth less near 50 than at the tails or vice versa depending on schedule; a model signal must clear fee-adjusted breakeven, not raw midpoint difference. Subtle: fee schedules change over time and by market type, so the version in force at trade time must be used.
m.fees.measurement: Version the fee formula from Kalshi's published fee schedule; compute breakeven probability per price and role; subtract from model edge before any threshold decision.
free_sources: Kalshi fee schedule PDF/help center (kalshi.com/fee-schedule) and /exchange/schedule API

m.lifecycle.label: Open/close/halt/postponement lifecycle events
m.lifecycle.mechanism: Market open, close, halts and postponement events determine when information can be traded on and which pregame snapshot is the last valid one.
m.lifecycle.rationale: Markets may close at scheduled start, on delay, or be extended; late-news windows (confirmed lineup/goalie) may fall before or after the close. Subtle: delayed or postponed games shift the effective decision time and can leave stale quotes, which also mislabels the 'closing' price used for CLV.
m.lifecycle.measurement: Record open_time, close_time, status transitions, and actual first pitch/puck drop from the league feed; define the last-valid-pregame timestamp as min(close_time, actual start); flag delayed/postponed games.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2: /markets, /markets/trades, /series/{series}/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks) /markets (open_time, close_time, status)

m.strike_hit_rates.label: Historical realized frequency by strike/rung per family (from settlements)
m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Realized frequency by rung gives the unconditional base rate that every conditional model must beat, and reveals persistent biases in how thresholds are set.
m.strike_hit_rates.rationale: Markets often over- or under-price specific rung shapes (round-number thresholds, longshot tails). Base rates by rung, season, venue and liquidity tier reveal where the market is calibrated and where it is not. Subtle: settled history is selection-biased by which strikes Kalshi chose to list, so rates are conditional on being listed.
m.strike_hit_rates.measurement: From settled markets compute hit rate by family x strike x price bucket with confidence intervals; compare to implied price; keep season and rule-version splits.

m.trade_tape.label: Executed trades (price, size, taker side, time) for slippage and flow
m.trade_tape.mechanism: Executed trades reveal where size actually transacted, the taker side, and the speed at which price reacts to news.
m.trade_tape.rationale: Trade flow around lineup/goalie/pitcher confirmation shows how quickly information is incorporated; sustained one-sided taker flow can indicate informed trading. Subtle: only executed prints are observable, resting orders are not, so slippage estimates from the tape understate the cost of crossing a thin book.
m.trade_tape.measurement: Pull trades per ticker with timestamps; compute signed volume (taker side), VWAP in windows around news timestamps, post-trade price drift as an informed-flow proxy; estimate slippage by size bucket.

mlb.season_sim_distribution.label: Season simulation distribution (division, wildcard, win totals)
mlb.season_sim_distribution.mechanism: Playoff and win-total markets are tails of a 162-game simulation with rating and injury uncertainty.
mlb.season_sim_distribution.rationale: A team's rating gives a mean win total; the market asks for tail probabilities that depend on schedule, correlation within divisions and injury attrition. Subtle: late-season motivation and resting change the last games.
mlb.season_sim_distribution.measurement: Monte Carlo of remaining games from own run-differential ratings (Pythagorean/BaseRuns shrunk), home advantage, starting-pitcher rotation uncertainty and tiebreaker rules; output win-total and playoff probabilities.

mlb.leader_order_statistic.label: Leader-race order statistic (home runs, strikeouts, batting titles)
mlb.leader_order_statistic.mechanism: The probability of leading is the chance a player's final total exceeds every rival's.
mlb.leader_order_statistic.rationale: Season-leader markets are max-of-N problems; to-date totals, games remaining, per-game rate variance and rival correlations (same park/schedule) set the probability. A projection of the mean is not enough: variance and the gap to the second place decide.
mlb.leader_order_statistic.measurement: Simulate each contender's remaining games from rate × playing-time distributions with injury hazards; compute the share of simulations in which he finishes first including ties.
free_sources: MLB StatsAPI leaderboards and game logs

mlb.clinched_rest_policy.label: Clinched/eliminated rest and call-up policy
mlb.clinched_rest_policy.mechanism: Teams with nothing to play for rest regulars and give opportunities to prospects.
mlb.clinched_rest_policy.rationale: Participation and counting-stat markets for regulars in the final weeks depend on the manager's historical behaviour once seeding is decided. The announcement is timestamped by lineup posting. Subtle: policy varies by manager and by whether a bye is at stake.
mlb.clinched_rest_policy.measurement: Per manager and season-state: share of regular starters sitting after clinch/elimination, by days remaining and bye status; compare with the lineup posted at decision time.

mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.label: Two-strike putaway decomposition: P(reach 2 strikes) x P(K | 2 strikes) by batter hand
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.mechanism: A strikeout needs two sub-events: the PA reaches a two-strike count, then the pitcher converts. The two pieces are driven by different pitches (first-pitch and early-count strikes versus chase/whiff pitches).
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.rationale: Aggregate K% and CSW hide that a pitcher can have a high K% from elite putaway on few two-strike PAs (fragile to lineup contact skill) or from reaching two strikes constantly (stable). Opposing hitters differ separately on 'gets to two strikes' (takes, fouls) and 'strikes out once there' (whiff on the chase pitch), so the matchup must be applied to each sub-event, not to the end rate.
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.measurement: For each pitcher, 3 seasons of pitch-level data with half-life 120 batters faced: r2 = share of PAs that reach 2 strikes (by batter hand); c2 = K / PAs reaching 2 strikes. For each batter: his own r2_b and c2_b, shrunk to league-by-hand with k = 150 PAs for r2 and k = 120 two-strike PAs for c2. Combine with odds-ratio (log5) per sub-event: logit(r2_match) = logit(r2_p) + logit(r2_b) - logit(r2_league), same for c2; matchup P(K) = r2_match * c2_match. Sum over the confirmed order weighted by expected PA per slot. Units: probability per PA; as-of the lineup-post timestamp using only games dated before the game.
free_sources: Baseball Savant / pybaseball Statcast pitch-level (balls, strikes, events)

mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.label: Starter removal hazard per batter faced (discrete-time survival curve)
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.mechanism: Batters faced is a first-passage time with removal hazard depending on pitch count, trip through the order, runs allowed and manager.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.rationale: The existing 'leash' label names the idea but gives no estimand. A K ladder cares about P(survive to batter 25+) and the hook is not a function of innings alone: a starter at 85 pitches with a 4-run deficit is removed at a different rate than one with a lead, and managers differ in whether they pull at the third-time-through boundary or at a pitch count. A measured hazard curve turns leash into a number the strikeout model can integrate over.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.measurement: Discrete-time logistic hazard h(b) = P(removed after batter b | still in) estimated on 5 seasons of starts (regular season; separate postseason intercept). Predictors: batters faced b (spline, knots at 9, 18, 27), pitch count (spline), runs allowed so far (0,1,2,3+), runners on at b, team lead/deficit bucket, days rest, season-to-date average pitches per start (shrunk to league with k = 8 starts), manager random effect (shrunk, k = 40 starts), bullpen-freshness index (relievers used last 2 days). Output: survival S(b) for b = 1..36 and E[BF]. As-of: manager and pitcher effects fit through the prior game; game-state predictors enter only inside a simulation, not as pregame data.

mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.label: Start-level dispersion of strikeouts beyond Poisson-binomial (rho parameter)
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.mechanism: Strikeouts across the nine batters share a pitcher-day latent state, so counts are more dispersed than independent Bernoulli draws.
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.rationale: The ladder prices neighbouring rungs from one distribution; if the variance is too small the 10+ and 11+ rungs are systematically underpriced and the 4+ rungs overpriced for high-K arms. A per-pitcher (or per-archetype) intra-start correlation parameter is the cheapest way to calibrate the width.
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.measurement: From 4 seasons of starts: for each start compute standardized residual of K given modelled expected K per batter faced (Pearson z = (K - sum p_i)/sqrt(sum p_i(1-p_i))). Estimate rho by moment matching: Var(K) = sum p_i(1-p_i) + rho*sum_{i!=j} sqrt(p_i(1-p_i)p_j(1-p_j)); pool pitchers by arsenal cluster (fastball-heavy, breaking-ball-heavy, finesse) and shrink to the pooled value with k = 25 starts. Report rho by cluster and by temperature bucket. As-of: estimated through the prior season, refreshed weekly in-season.

mlb.battery_assignment.label: Pitcher-catcher battery effect (actual catcher assigned) on K%-over-expected
mlb.battery_assignment.mechanism: The catcher selected for the start changes framing, pitch-calling and blocking; some pitchers have personal catchers.
mlb.battery_assignment.rationale: Existing catcher_framing is a team-season catcher metric; what moves a single start is which catcher is in the lineup card and whether the pitcher is paired with him. Backup catchers have a materially different framing level and often start day games after night games, so it is partly predictable from the schedule.
mlb.battery_assignment.measurement: For each pitcher-catcher pair over 3 seasons: K%-over-expected = (K - sum p_i)/BF using the matchup-model expectation excluding the catcher; shrink the pair effect to the catcher's overall framing runs per 1000 called pitches with k = 250 BF. Pre-lineup: P(catcher = c) from the team's rotation of catchers conditioned on rest pattern; post-lineup: realised catcher. Units: K probability points per BF. As-of: lineup post timestamp.

mlb.abs_challenge_regime.label: ABS challenge-system zone regime (2026+): effective zone, challenge availability and success, catcher/batter challenge skill
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.mechanism: With automated ball-strike challenges, a borderline pitch can be overturned to the true zone, so called-strike probability on edge pitches, framing value and umpire zone effects shrink toward the robotic zone and challenge skill matters.
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.rationale: Every 2026 regular-season and postseason game (including the sampled Oct 28 2026 game) uses challenges (two per team, successful ones retained, extra challenges in extras), so strikeout-looking events, count leverage and framing value differ from the human-umpire seasons that supply most history; umpire and framing effects estimated on 2021-2025 do not transfer unchanged.
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.measurement: From 2026 pitch-level data compute for each pitcher-catcher pair (a) share of borderline pitches (within 1.5 inches of the zone edge) called strikes after challenges, (b) challenge rate and overturn rate when the battery or the batter challenges, shrunk to league with k = 30 challenges, (c) the 2026 league difference in called-strike rate on edge pitches versus 2025. Replace umpire_k_bb_effect and framing priors with 2025-weighted estimates multiplied by the 2026 edge-pitch shrink factor (ratio of 2026 to 2025 edge called-strike variance across umpires). Units: change in K probability per batter. As-of: through prior games; 2026 data accumulate during the season.
free_sources: Baseball Savant pitch-level data with ABS challenge fields (assumed present in 2026 exports, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
MLB Stats API gamefeed review events

mlb.exit_boundary_mass.label: Manager exit-boundary mass: P(removal at outs = 3k | reached) with run-state conditioning
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.mechanism: Starter removals cluster at inning boundaries and at the start of the third time through, and each manager has a characteristic exit lattice.
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.rationale: Outs ladders sit on multiples of three; if removals are smooth, P(outs>=15) and P(outs>=16) are priced alike, but if the manager lets starters finish innings then 16-17 outs are rare while 15 and 18 carry mass. Existing leash does not carry this discreteness.
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.measurement: For every start in the last 4 seasons record exit_outs. For each manager m (current manager only; reset on change) estimate P(exit_outs = j | outs reached j-? ) for j in {3,6,...,24} separately for pitch-count bucket (<85, 85-100, >100) and run-state bucket (starter leading, tied or trailing by <=2, trailing by >=3). Shrink to league conditional with k = 30 starts per cell. Output the conditional distribution of exit_outs for the listed pitcher (rows) by combining with his expected pitch rate per out. As-of: through the previous game.
free_sources: Retrosheet game logs and event files

mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.label: Outs per batter faced including double plays and baserunning outs
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.mechanism: Outs are not one per batter: GIDP adds a second out, and caught stealing and pickoffs add outs without a PA.
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.rationale: Using one minus OBP per batter understates outs for ground-ball pitchers with a double-play-prone lineup and a runner on first; it also ignores that reach-on-error and fielder's choice change who is out. This is the pitcher-level conversion that links batters faced to outs.
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.measurement: outs_per_BF = (1 - P(H) - P(BB) - P(HBP) - P(ROE) - P(FC reach)) + P(GIDP|BF) + (CS+PO outs)/BF. Compute pitcher-side P(GIDP) = P(GB) x P(runner on 1B, <2 out) x lineup DP rate (GIDP per opportunity of the confirmed batters, shrunk to league with k = 100 opportunities). Pitcher rates over 2 seasons half-life 300 BF, shrink k = 250 BF to league-by-handedness. Baserunning outs per BF from pickoff/CS counts with catcher arm and runner speed. Units: outs per batter. As-of: lineup post timestamp.

mlb.delay_starter_removal.label: Rain-delay interruption hazard and starter-removal-after-delay rule
mlb.delay_starter_removal.mechanism: A long weather delay usually ends the starter's night; outs are frozen at the delay.
mlb.delay_starter_removal.rationale: Weather appears in the existing catalog only as heat and generic delay; the outs outcome has an explicit truncation that depends on delay length and on whether the manager returns the starter. In rain-prone parks with open roofs the interruption probability is not trivial and shifts the middle rungs.
mlb.delay_starter_removal.measurement: P(in-game delay >= 30 min) = forecast precipitation/lightning probability in innings 2-6 window x roof-open indicator x park-level conversion rate from historical forecast-to-delay (fit on 5 seasons, logistic with intercept by park). P(starter does not return | delay length L) = logistic in L (fit on observed delays: L<30, 30-60, >60) with manager effect shrunk k = 15 delays. Output expected truncation probability by inning. As-of: 3 hours pre-first-pitch forecast vintage and again at lineup post.
free_sources: MLB Stats API game status and delay durations

mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.label: Confirmed opposing batting order out-rate profile: OBP, strikeout, ground-ball double-play and speed by slot against the starter's hand
mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.mechanism: Outs per batter faced depend on the nine specific hitters: on-base skill lowers outs per PA, strikeouts and grounders into double plays raise them.
mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.rationale: The outs ladder converts batters faced into outs; a lineup of high-OBP, low-GIDP hitters can cost two or three outs over a start relative to a free-swinging lineup, and the order of the hitters changes who bats with runners on. The lineup posts a few hours before first pitch, so the input has a vintage problem.
mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.measurement: For each of the nine confirmed slots take projected out probability per PA = 1 - OBP_proj(vs starter hand) + GIDP_rate x P(runner on first with <2 outs) (ZiPS/Steamer shrunk to 2-season stats with k = 300 PA), weighted by expected PA through the starter's modelled batters faced (slot PA weights 4.65 down to 3.85 per game, truncated to the starter's expected BF). Output: expected outs per batter faced for the lineup (about 0.68-0.72 league) and its deviation from league; units outs per BF. As-of: lineup post; before it, a mixture over the team's usual orders.

mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.label: ABS-regime effect on pitches per plate appearance and walk rate (2026+)
mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.mechanism: Under automated ball-strike challenges the called zone on borderline pitches is more consistent, shifting walks, called strikes and therefore pitch cost per out relative to the human-umpire seasons that supply history.
mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.rationale: Pitches per PA is a history-based average and cannot contain the day's zone regime; all 2026 games use ABS challenges, which changes walks and called strikes. The pitch budget that caps outs depends on pitches per out, so an unmodelled regime shift mis-states the ceiling.
mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.measurement: From 2026 pitch-level data compute league and pitcher-level changes versus 2025 in (a) pitches per PA, (b) BB rate, (c) called-strike share of borderline pitches, with shrinkage of the pitcher-level shift toward the league shift using k = 150 PA; apply the shift to pre-2026 pitches-per-PA priors. Units: pitches per PA and walk probability. As-of: through prior games; 2026 sample builds over the season.

mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.label: Run-expectancy conversion of baserunners (RE24-allowed by base-out state, pitcher profile)
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.mechanism: Earned runs equal the sum of run-value increments across base-out states; HR and extra-base hits convert traffic to runs.
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.rationale: LOB% regression treats strand rate as luck, but strand rate partly reflects pitcher skill (K and GB with runners on) and HR timing. A direct PA-level run-expectancy accounting separates how many baserunners a pitcher allows from how many each is worth.
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.measurement: For each pitcher over 2 seasons (half-life 400 BF): runs per baserunner = (runs allowed charged) / (H + BB + HBP); decompose with RE24 table: for each PA, delta RE given outcome. Fit pitcher-specific outcome probabilities by base-out state (K with runners on, GB with runner on first, HR/FB), shrink to league with k = 250 BF. Expected ER for the lineup = sum over PAs from a Markov simulation using these state-dependent outcomes and the confirmed batting order; subtract expected unearned share (see er_ur_scoring_split). Units: runs per 9 innings equivalent, then per BF. As-of: lineup post.
free_sources: Statcast events with runners on base and outs

mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.label: Expected unearned-run share (team errors, passed balls, catcher and infield error rates)
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.mechanism: Runs after an error or passed ball that extends an inning can be unearned and are not counted.
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.rationale: Earned runs are what the contract pays on; runs can differ. Teams with poor infield defense or a passed-ball-prone catcher have a larger gap, and an error that extends an inning raises the number of batters faced and baserunners without adding earned runs.
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.measurement: Per team: unearned runs per game over last 2 seasons half-life 60 games, regress to league mean with k = 40 games. Per pitcher: share of runs unearned over 3 seasons with k = 300 BF. Adjust for the confirmed fielders (error rate per ball in play by position) and the confirmed catcher (passed ball + wild pitch per 100 innings). Expected ER = expected R x (1 - unearned_share). Units: fraction of runs. As-of lineup post.
free_sources: Retrosheet / Baseball-Reference fielding and error data

mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.label: Inherited-runner charge risk after starter exit (expected extra earned runs)
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.mechanism: A starter is charged for runners left on base when relieved, so the bullpen strand rate determines part of his earned runs.
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.rationale: The starter's earned-run count is not finished when he leaves: if he leaves with traffic and the reliever allows them to score, those runs are his. Exit-with-traffic probability is high in blow-up outings, the same outings that populate the right tail of the ER ladder.
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.measurement: P(exit with k runners) from the hazard model (see leash) x P(each inherited runner scores | reliever profile) with reliever strand rate shrunk to league (k = 60 BF with inherited runners). Expected extra ER = sum_k P(k) x k x p_score x (1-unearned share). Use the likely first reliever from bullpen availability (setup man or long man). Units: expected earned runs added. As-of: lineup post + bullpen usage from prior 2 days.

mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.label: Scorer hit/error tendency by park (borderline play calls)
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.mechanism: Hits depend on official scorer rulings at the hit/error margin.
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.rationale: In some parks the scorer rules more plays errors than average, converting would-be hits into unearned reached-base events; changes made after the game may alter settlement values.
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.measurement: Per home park: hit-or-error ruling rate on batted balls with similar expected out probability (xBA bucket) vs league, over 3 seasons with k = 200 plays shrinkage; flag later rulings changes. Units: probability shift in hit given contact bucket. As-of: through prior game. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: scorer identity per game is not confirmed as a public pregame field. CAVEAT: no evidence is cited that scorer identity persists as a tendency; default to park-level hit/error rates and treat scorer identity as a hypothesis to test.

mlb.abs_zone_walk_effect.label: ABS-regime effect on walk and run-scoring probability (2026+): borderline-pitch call share and challenge outcomes
mlb.abs_zone_walk_effect.mechanism: Walks come from called balls and strikes; automated challenges on borderline pitches change the called-strike share and the value of framing and umpire zones relative to human-umpire history.
mlb.abs_zone_walk_effect.rationale: Every 2026 game uses ABS challenges, so the walks ladder and the baserunner volume feeding earned runs depend on a zone regime for which UmpScorecards and catcher-framing history are only a prior; the convex walk response to the called-strike share makes small regime shifts matter at the 3+ walks rung.
mlb.abs_zone_walk_effect.measurement: From 2026 pitch-level data estimate the league and pitcher-battery change versus 2025 in BB rate on borderline-pitch counts: delta_BB = BB%_2026 - BB%_2025 at matched count and zone-edge mix, shrunk toward the league delta with k = 150 PA per pitcher. Rescale pre-2026 umpire and framing coefficients by the ratio of 2026 to 2025 edge-pitch called-strike spread. Units: walk probability per PA. As-of: through prior games.
free_sources: MLB Stats API gamefeed review events

mlb.late_replacement_risk.label: Early-removal and pinch-hit-for risk for a starting hitter (PA truncation)
mlb.late_replacement_risk.mechanism: A starter may be lifted for a pinch hitter or defensive replacement, so PA count is truncated and the late PAs against the bullpen go to someone else.
mlb.late_replacement_risk.rationale: Slot-based PA expectations assume a full game; platoon players, catchers and aging regulars are routinely removed in high-leverage late innings or in blowouts, and the settlement counts only the starter's own PAs.
mlb.late_replacement_risk.measurement: For each hitter-season: P(removed before PA k) for k = 3,4,5 estimated from game logs: indicator that the hitter has fewer than k PAs when the team completed at least k-1 times through the order, by team score state (lead>=4, within 3, trail>=4) and opposing reliever hand. Shrink hitter rate to role-class (everyday, platoon, catcher, veteran DH) with k = 60 games. Output vector of survival probabilities to PA3, PA4, PA5. As-of: confirmed lineup + pregame total.

mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.label: Expected PA split against the starter versus relievers with reliever handedness
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.mechanism: Later PAs are against relievers, often of the batter's weaker platoon side, so the hitter's per-PA rate differs for PA 1-3 versus 4-5.
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.rationale: Team-level bullpen talent hides which relievers the batter faces; the batter faces a distribution over reliever identities determined by starter exit time and managerial matchup use, which changes both handedness and quality.
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.measurement: From the hazard of starter exit (see pitcher archetypes) compute expected PA index at exit for each lineup slot; allocate remaining PAs to the likely bullpen sequence (closer excluded from innings before 9 unless lead is close) with reliever platoon shares by team/manager over last 2 seasons. Per-PA probabilities = batter splits vs the hand distribution; shrink batter-vs-hand splits to hitter overall with k = 200 PA vs same-hand and 400 PA vs opposite-hand. Units: expected PA vs starter, expected PA vs LHP relief, vs RHP relief. As-of: lineup post + bullpen availability.

mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.label: Batted-ball outcome model P(1B, 2B, 3B, HR | exit velocity, launch angle, spray, park, defense)
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.mechanism: Total bases weights outcomes 1-4, so per-hit and per-PA probabilities of each outcome type, not just hit probability, drive TB rungs.
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.rationale: xBA and xSLG are season-aggregate and park-neutral; a single game needs the outcome mix given the actual park, handedness and the opposing defense. Doubles and triples depend on spray and park geometry (gap depth, wall height) and on runner speed, and HR depends on the carry.
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.measurement: Fit a multinomial model on 4 seasons of batted-ball events: outcome ~ spline(launch_speed, launch_angle) x spray_angle x park (random effect) x batter hand x fielder alignment indicator (post-2023 shift limits). For each hitter compute his batted-ball distribution (EV, LA, spray) over 2 seasons half-life 200 BIP with shrinkage to hand-class k = 150 BIP, then expected outcome mix for the game park. Expected TB per PA = P(K)=0 + sum outcome probability x bases; units bases per PA. As-of: lineup post.
free_sources: FanGraphs park factors by hit type

mlb.park_specific_xhr.label: Park-and-weather-specific expected home runs per fly ball (xHR by batted-ball sector)
mlb.park_specific_xhr.mechanism: Whether a hit fly ball clears the wall depends on distance, wall height in that sector, wind component, air density and roof.
mlb.park_specific_xhr.rationale: A park HR factor averages over all sprays; a pull-heavy hitter in a park with a short porch on his pull side gets a very different factor from a spray hitter. Deviation from the average on a specific day (wind out to right) matters most for hitters who hit to that sector.
mlb.park_specific_xhr.measurement: From 4 seasons of batted balls with exit velocity, launch angle and spray angle, fit P(HR | EV, LA, spray) per park by logistic spline with park random effect; add wind component along the spray direction and air density as covariates. For each hitter compute expected HR per fly ball by integrating his empirical (EV, LA, spray) distribution (half-life 200 BIP, shrink to hand-class k = 150 BIP) over the game park with the day's wind and density. Units: probability per batted ball and per PA. As-of: forecast at lineup post.
free_sources: park wall geometry (Ballparks of Baseball / team sites)

mlb.relief_hr_vulnerability_by_hand.label: Expected reliever HR vulnerability by hand for the PAs after the starter exits
mlb.relief_hr_vulnerability_by_hand.mechanism: Later PAs face relievers whose HR rate and handedness differ from the starter's.
mlb.relief_hr_vulnerability_by_hand.rationale: HR rates of relievers are not the starter's; relief pitchers are often fastball-heavy but with lower HR/FB, and managers match hands. For a batter with 4 PAs, one or two come against relievers so ignoring them mis-sets the late-PA HR probability.
mlb.relief_hr_vulnerability_by_hand.measurement: Using the starter-exit survival, allocate PA index to likely relievers (top 3-4 by team usage in last 20 games, by hand). Reliever HR rate per PA vs same-hand and opposite-hand batters over 2 seasons half-life 250 BF, shrink to league relief by hand with k = 200 BF. Per-hitter HR probability for PA >= k = hitter power x reliever vulnerability. Units: HR per PA. As-of: bullpen availability at lineup post.

mlb.series_hr_exposure.label: Series home-run exposure: games played distribution x start probability x per-game HR rate
mlb.series_hr_exposure.mechanism: A series HR total is an aggregation over a random number of games in which the hitter may or may not start.
mlb.series_hr_exposure.rationale: The 2+ HR series rung is dominated by how many games the series goes (4-7) and whether the hitter plays each; the per-game HR probability then compounds. Team playoffs and rest days change both exposure and opposing starters (aces vs fifth starter).
mlb.series_hr_exposure.measurement: N_games ~ distribution from series win-prob model (probability each game, length distribution 4-7 for best-of-7); P(start) per game from role (everyday = 0.95, platoon = 0.55 conditional on opposing starter hand); per-game p_HR from the single-game model with each game's probable starter. Series count distribution = compound sum. Units: expected HR in series. As-of: before each game with updated series state.

mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.label: Within-game shared HR environment dispersion (wind/ball/pitcher day latent)
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.mechanism: Home runs by different hitters in the same game share environment and pitcher states, so counts are overdispersed relative to independent Bernoullis.
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.rationale: Single-hitter markets need only his marginal, but any multi-hitter or team inference (and the 2+ HR rung) depends on positive dependence; wind blowing out raises everyone's probability together and HR events cluster when a pitcher is lacking command.
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.measurement: From 4 seasons of games compute the variance ratio of team-plus-opponent HR counts to the Poisson-binomial expectation given the matchup model, by park roof type and wind-out strength decile; estimate dispersion phi (negative binomial) shrunk to league with k = 100 games. Units: variance inflation. As-of: through prior games. FALLBACK (pre-registered, no matchup model needed): estimate phi first from league-average HR per PA by park, roof type and wind-out decile using plate-appearance counts, then replace expectation with the project's matchup model once it exists; the two-step version avoids circularity.

mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.label: Playoff walk-off count: remaining-games exposure and per-game walk-off probability
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.mechanism: A walk-off is a home-team win in the bottom of the 9th or an extra inning; the playoff count is the sum over remaining playoff games of a Bernoulli event whose probability depends on late-inning state, closer quality and who is home.
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.rationale: KXMLBWALKOFFS pays on at least N walk-offs across the playoffs (the run that gives the home team the lead ends the game), so it is a count over a random number of games, with the count so far fixed. The per-game probability is not constant: it needs the home team to be tied or trailing by a small margin entering its last at-bat and to score the go-ahead run, and it varies with bullpen quality, extras probability and home-team identity.
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.measurement: Count so far W0 from official game results. Remaining games G are random: enumerate bracket paths and series lengths (best-of-5 or 7) from own per-game win probabilities. For each future game compute p_walkoff = P(home team trails by <=3 or is tied entering the bottom of the 9th and takes the lead before three outs, or wins in an extra inning) from the game run model plus half-inning chain with the visiting closer and due-up slots (walk-off stopping rule), shrunk to the league postseason rate over 2015-2025 with k = 100 games. P(count >= N) = P(W0 + sum Bernoulli(p_g) >= N) integrated over the distribution of G (Poisson-binomial mixture). Units: count and probability. As-of: daily during the playoffs.
free_sources: MLB Stats API postseason schedule and linescores

mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.label: Per-PA base-out state distribution from the confirmed lineup (Markov chain)
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.mechanism: RBI opportunity is the probability distribution of runners and outs when the hitter bats, derived from the hitters ahead.
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.rationale: Average RBI opportunity per slot hides lineup-specific variation: the same cleanup hitter has materially more RBI chances behind two .380-OBP hitters than behind two .300-OBP hitters, and opposing starter baserunner allowance scales it.
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.measurement: Build a nine-state-by-outs Markov chain for the confirmed lineup: transition probabilities per batter (P(1B), P(2B), P(HR), P(BB/HBP), P(K), P(GB DP), P(out other)) from batter true-talent shrunk to league with k = 200 PA and adjusted to the opposing starter and park. Run 10k simulated games or solve analytically to get P(runner on 1B, 2B, 3B; outs) at each of the hitter's PAs; summarise as expected runner-weighted opportunity (sum over runners aboard). Units: expected runners on base per PA. As-of: lineup post.

mlb.rbi_conversion_by_runner_base.label: RBI conversion rate by runner position (1B/2B/3B) and outs, excluding GIDP
mlb.rbi_conversion_by_runner_base.mechanism: Given runners, the hitter's chance to drive them in differs by base and outs and includes sacrifice flies, productive outs and HR.
mlb.rbi_conversion_by_runner_base.rationale: A batter's RBI per runner on base differs for a power hitter (HR clears everyone) versus a contact hitter (scores runner from third on a fly ball) versus a ground-ball hitter (GIDP, no RBI). Aggregated RBI/PA mixes these roles with opportunity.
mlb.rbi_conversion_by_runner_base.measurement: For each hitter over 3 seasons: RBI per runner-on-base-PA split by (3B-only, 2B/3B, 1B-only, bases loaded) x outs (0, 1, 2) from event data; shrink each cell to hand-class cell with k = 40 opportunities. Components: P(HR | state), P(hit | state) and RISP contact rate, P(sac fly | runner 3B, <2 out), P(GIDP | runner 1B, <2 out). Units: expected RBI per PA given state. As-of: through prior game.

mlb.sb_opportunity_conversion.label: Steal attempt hazard per opportunity (runner on first, second base open) by game state
mlb.sb_opportunity_conversion.mechanism: A steal attempt is a decision at each opportunity influenced by runner, battery, score and rule regime.
mlb.sb_opportunity_conversion.rationale: Season SB totals mix opportunity (how often the runner reaches first) with decision and success; the contract is per game so opportunity is the pivotal driver, and the decision probability depends on score margin (late blowouts suppress steals), pitcher hand and the pickoff-disengagement rule.
mlb.sb_opportunity_conversion.measurement: For each runner over 2 seasons (2023+ rule regime only): attempts / opportunities where opportunity = PA-end or between-PA state with runner on first and second open and fewer than two outs; stratify by pitcher hand (L/R), score margin (|margin|<=3 vs >3) and inning (<=6, >=7). Shrink to speed-class rate with k = 30 opportunities. Multiply by P(opportunity) = P(reach first) from lineup chain and by success probability (runner success rate vs battery pop time + time to plate, shrunk k = 25 attempts). Units: steals per game. As-of: lineup post (catcher and pitcher known).
free_sources: Baseball Savant running splits and sprint speed
Statcast pop time and pitcher time to plate

mlb.batting_behind_protection.label: Quality of the hitters batting behind (on-deck and following) as a pitch-around and intentional-walk driver
mlb.batting_behind_protection.mechanism: Pitchers and managers decide whether to pitch to or around a hitter, and whether to hold or send a runner, based on who follows; a weak hitter on deck raises walks and intentional walks for the current hitter and lowers his RBI chances.
mlb.batting_behind_protection.rationale: RBI conversion and steal attempts both depend on the batter behind: with first base open a dangerous on-deck hitter lowers the walk rate, while a weak one invites intentional walks that remove RBI chances. This is stated only in interactions today and has no measurable input; it also changes the green light for a runner on first.
mlb.batting_behind_protection.measurement: For hitter h in slot s of the confirmed lineup, compute protection = mean projected wOBA (vs the starter's hand, shrunk to ZiPS/Steamer with k = 300 PA) of the next two hitters in the order, minus the league mean wOBA, in wOBA points. Convert to expected intentional-plus-unintentional walk-rate shift using a regression of BB% on protection with first-base-open flag over 2021-2025 (shrunk by hitter with k = 200 PA). Output: change in per-PA walk probability and in the P(runner goes) at first base. As-of: lineup post.
free_sources: Retrosheet event files (first-base-open flag, intentional walks)

mlb.lineup_strength_delta.label: Day-specific lineup strength delta (confirmed lineup vs team baseline, in runs per game)
mlb.lineup_strength_delta.mechanism: The nine hitters who actually play differ from the team's season baseline because of rest days, platoon choices and injuries.
mlb.lineup_strength_delta.rationale: Team-level wRC+ averages across the season's lineups; the confirmed card might lack its best hitter or contain a bench bat, and the effect is not uniform across the order (top slots get more PAs).
mlb.lineup_strength_delta.measurement: delta (runs per game) = sum over slots s of PA_share(s) x (wOBA_proj(hitter_s, vs starter hand) - wOBA_proj(team regular at slot s)) / wOBA_scale, with wOBA_scale about 1.2 (so 0.100 team-wide wOBA over about 38 PA is about 3.2 runs); PA_share already sums to about 38.2 PA per game, so no further 9-inning multiplier is applied. Projections from rest-of-season systems (ZiPS/Steamer) blended with 2-season xwOBA shrunk to projection k = 300 PA. PA_share from slot PA expectations (4.65, 4.55, 4.45, 4.35, 4.25, 4.15, 4.05, 3.95, 3.85). Units: runs per game. As-of: lineup post.

mlb.home_field_run_advantage.label: Park-specific home-field effect (win-probability and run advantage) with last-at-bat component
mlb.home_field_run_advantage.mechanism: Home teams win more often than road teams: last at-bat, familiarity, travel and umpire exposure.
mlb.home_field_run_advantage.rationale: A constant HFA hides park differences (dimensions, sightlines, altitude familiarity) and the structural last-at-bat advantage that produces extra home wins in tied late innings and truncates the bottom-9th when the home team leads.
mlb.home_field_run_advantage.measurement: Estimate team-home (HFA_t) via mixed model on 10 seasons: run margin ~ team strength (home + away) + home indicator + park random effect (shrunk k = 400 games per park) + travel-days indicator; add last-at-bat component = P(home wins | tied entering 9th) - 0.5 from extras data. Output HFA in run margin and win probability for the specific park. As-of: through prior season plus current.

mlb.late_inning_leverage_deployment.label: Reliever deployment by lead size (who pitches innings 7-9 as a function of margin) and its run-prevention effect
mlb.late_inning_leverage_deployment.mechanism: Managers use high-leverage relievers in close games and low-leverage arms in blowouts, compressing and lumpifying the margin.
mlb.late_inning_leverage_deployment.rationale: A margin spread cover is not a symmetric diffusion: leads of one to three runs are protected by the best bullpen arms while four-plus leads are mopped up by weaker arms, so favorites win by exactly one or two more often than a normal model suggests.
mlb.late_inning_leverage_deployment.measurement: For each team over the last 2 seasons: runs allowed per inning in innings 7-9 by lead bucket (tie/within1, 2-3, 4+) and by reliever tier (top-3 by leverage index vs rest). Shrink bucket runs allowed to league with k = 100 innings. Combine with the margin distribution through a Markov simulation in innings 7-9: P(margin change | state). Units: run-allowed rate by state. As-of: bullpen availability at lineup post.
free_sources: MLB Stats API play-by-play (leverage index, pitching changes)

mlb.regular_season_stakes_and_rest_polic.label: Regular-season stakes and rest policy (clinched/eliminated status, rest-day probabilities, September roster behaviour)
mlb.regular_season_stakes_and_rest_polic.mechanism: Teams that have clinched or been eliminated rest regulars, shorten starters' leashes or run tryout lineups, which lowers team strength on that day relative to the full-strength baseline.
mlb.regular_season_stakes_and_rest_polic.rationale: Late-season games for clinched or eliminated teams are played by different hitters and a differently managed bullpen than the season-long ratings assume; lineup_strength_delta only sees this after the card posts, while starter handling and bullpen usage in meaningless games never flow through it. Postseason games have no such effect, so the input must be gated by game type.
mlb.regular_season_stakes_and_rest_polic.measurement: For each team-game compute (a) playoff-clinch and elimination flags from standings (magic number <= games remaining, or tragic number), (b) games_since_last_rest_day for each of the 9 regular-lineup hitters and their historical P(sit) when the team is clinched/eliminated/in a day-game-after-night-game, estimated over the prior 5 seasons with shrinkage k = 40 team-games, (c) starter innings expectation reduced by the team's historical clinched/eliminated leash shift. Output: expected regular-lineup PA share and expected starter innings; units are PA share and innings. As-of: the morning of the game, updated at lineup post. Set to neutral for postseason games.
free_sources: MLB Stats API standings and schedule

mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.label: Probability the home team's bottom of the ninth is skipped (home lead after 8.5) and its run-total effect
mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.mechanism: A home team ahead after the top of the ninth does not bat, so its runs and the game total are truncated relative to nine full innings.
mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.rationale: A total of 8.5 is often priced as if both teams bat nine innings; in games where the home team is ahead the home runs stop early, shifting probability toward under, and the truncation is correlated with favorite status and low total.
mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.measurement: P(skip) = P(home leads after 8.5 innings) from the run distribution: P(home leads after top of 9) computed by convolving inning-level scores through 8 innings plus the visitors' top-9 distribution. Expected truncation loss in total = P(skip) x E[home runs in a bottom-9 inning] (about 0.5 runs). Adjust the mean total by that amount and widen the lower tail. As-of: lineup post with projected win probability. Units: runs of expected truncation. WALK-OFF TRUNCATION: when the home team trails or is tied entering the bottom of the 9th (or an extra inning), the half-inning ends once it takes the lead, so remaining runs are lost; compute the home team's expected runs in that half under the stopping rule (capped at runs needed plus the homer exception) and apply the loss separately to the home team total (KXMLBTEAMTOTAL for the home side), which is truncated, versus the visitor total, which is not, and to the combined game total.

mlb.extras_run_contribution.label: Expected runs added by extra innings, by rule regime (regular-season automatic runner vs postseason bases-empty) and contract scope
mlb.extras_run_contribution.mechanism: A game tied after nine adds extra half-innings; in the regular season each starts with a runner on second, in the postseason (to my knowledge, unverified for 2026) each starts with bases empty, so the runs added differ by regime; runs there count only if the contract counts them.
mlb.extras_run_contribution.rationale: About one game in ten adds a few runs, which matters for rungs near the median; if the contract excludes extras, then these runs must be removed and shortened-game and walk-off logic differ.
mlb.extras_run_contribution.measurement: E[extras runs] = P(level after nine complete innings) x E[total runs in extras | level]. Estimate runs per extra half-inning by regime: regular season with automatic runner (2020-2025 extras, about 0.9-1.1 runs per half-inning, shrunk to team offence with k = 50 half-innings); postseason or any bases-empty extras at about the league per-inning rate for tied late-inning bullpens (about 0.45-0.55 runs per half-inning, estimated from postseason and pre-2020 extra innings). The home half ends at the go-ahead run (walk-off stopping rule), so the home half contributes fewer runs than the visitor half. Use the regime flag from the game type (regular season vs postseason) and set to 0 if rules say regulation only. Units: expected runs. As-of: lineup post and contract text version.
free_sources: Retrosheet / MLB Stats API extra-inning data

mlb.series_length_distribution.label: Series length distribution (probability of 4/5/6/7 games) from game-level win probabilities with team-strength dependence
mlb.series_length_distribution.mechanism: A series total contract settles on how many games are played, a function of game win probabilities, home-field pattern and the dependence of games on a shared team-strength latent.
mlb.series_length_distribution.rationale: Using independent Bernoulli games understates the probability of sweeps and long series; team strength uncertainty and starter rotation make the sequence dependent, and short series compress the talent gap.
mlb.series_length_distribution.measurement: Simulate best-of-seven: game i win prob p_i from the single-game model with announced starters and rest (default 2-3-2 home pattern), draw team-strength offset ~ N(0, sd = 0.04 in win prob) shared across games, compute P(N=4,5,6,7). P(7 games)=1 - P(<=6). Calibrate sd to historical series length frequency (best-of-7 series since 2012). As-of: after each game with updated series state.
free_sources: Game-level win probability from team model

mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.label: Probability the listed starter does not start (scratch, opener, bulk swap) and replacement distribution
mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.mechanism: F5 contracts do not condition on the pitcher, so a change shifts the whole distribution.
mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.rationale: Pre-lineup prices sit on the announced pitcher; a late scratch or opener plan is a large run-expectation change (a quality starter replaced by a bullpen day), and in the postseason pitching plans change.
mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.measurement: P(change) = logistic on days-to-game, pitcher status (IL return, injury flag, workload), team plan flags (opener/bulk usage rate in last 10 starts), postseason indicator; calibrate on 5 seasons of announced-versus-actual starters. Replacement distribution = mixture over the plausible alternates (next in rotation, bulk reliever, opener) with their F5 run rates. As-of: at each time before first pitch. Units: probability and expected F5 runs shift. CALIBRATION CAVEAT: announced-versus-actual starter history is not archived by free feeds (see unresolved f5_probable_vintage); until own capture accumulates a season, the change probability is a prior from league base rates, not a calibrated estimate.
free_sources: MLB Stats API probable pitchers history (vintage unverified)

mlb.f5_lineup_slot_exposure.label: Expected plate appearances by slot in innings 1-5 and slot-weighted matchup runs
mlb.f5_lineup_slot_exposure.mechanism: Within five innings the top of each order bats twice and the bottom less, so slots receive unequal weight.
mlb.f5_lineup_slot_exposure.rationale: Full-game wRC+ weights nine slots roughly evenly; F5 weight shifts toward the top six, and the weight on the top varies with team OBP (more baserunners, more PAs).
mlb.f5_lineup_slot_exposure.measurement: Markov-chain expected PA by slot in 5 innings given lineup OBP and starter allowed OBP: roughly (2.75, 2.65, 2.6, 2.5, 2.4, 2.3, 2.2, 2.1, 2.0) for a typical team, which sums to the team total of about 21.5 PA in five innings (about 4.3 PA per inning); slot weights are normalised to sum to the modelled team PA total. Slot-weighted runs per PA = sum slot weight x hitter run value vs starter hand (projection wOBA, k = 300 PA shrinkage). Units: expected runs in 5 innings against a typical starter. As-of: lineup post.

mlb.f5_reliever_innings_share.label: Expected share of the first five innings thrown by relievers (early exit) and their quality
mlb.f5_reliever_innings_share.mechanism: Early starter exits push relievers into innings 4 and 5; the mixture shifts F5 runs.
mlb.f5_reliever_innings_share.rationale: Starter-only models understate runs when the starter has a short leash, and bullpen quality (not starter) then governs the end of the F5 window; openers make the share large.
mlb.f5_reliever_innings_share.measurement: From the starter hazard of exit (see leash) compute E[outs by reliever in innings 1-5] = 15 - E[min(starter outs, 15)]; relief quality from the likely first reliever and leverage; F5 reliever share = that/15. F5 runs = starter rate x share_starter + reliever rate x share_relief. Uses 5 seasons start logs, k = 8 starts shrinkage to team average. Units: outs and runs per out. As-of: lineup post.

mlb.first_inning_markov_run_prob.label: First-inning run probability from a base-out Markov chain with the confirmed top-4 hitters and the starter's first-trip PA outcome rates
mlb.first_inning_markov_run_prob.mechanism: RFI is the union of two half-innings; each is a Markov process over the first four or five hitters.
mlb.first_inning_markov_run_prob.rationale: First-inning ERA or RFI history is nearly pure noise; a chain built from PA-level outcome probabilities (not inning-level results) uses all the data and the confirmed order, and includes the fact that the fourth and fifth hitters bat only if the first three reach.
mlb.first_inning_markov_run_prob.measurement: For each half-inning: transition probabilities for batter slots 1-5 from log5-combined P(walk), P(1B), P(2B+), P(HR), P(K), P(other out) using hitter vs hand rates (shrunk to projection k = 250 PA) and starter first-time-through rates (starter first-trip PA outcomes over last 2 seasons, shrunk to league k = 300 BF). Solve the chain analytically: P(no run) = path probabilities to three outs without scoring. RFI = 1 - P(no run top) x P(no run bottom); P(top run) and P(bottom run) also output for team-specific markets. Units: probability. As-of: lineup post.

mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.label: Ninth-inning entry state (score margin, home-bats flag) and expected pitcher and due-up slots
mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.mechanism: The 9th inning's run distribution depends on whether the home team bats, the margin, and who pitches.
mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.rationale: KXMLBINNINGTOTAL and KXMLBINNINGWIN settle on the ninth only, including the case where the home team skips the bottom. The probability that the bottom of the ninth is played falls with home-team lead probability, and the pitcher is the closer in save situations or a mop-up arm in blowouts.
mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher.measurement: P(home bats bottom 9) = P(home not leading after top 9) from the run distribution after 8 innings and top-9 runs. Margin entering 9 from simulated score distribution (innings 1-8). Pitcher: P(closer) = P(save situation: lead 1-3 for the home team entering visitor's top? (visitors pitching vs home)); for the visitor's top 9 the pitcher is the home team's closer if home leads by <=3, otherwise a setup/mop-up arm. Closer availability from usage in prior 2 days (back-to-back/3-in-4 flags). Due-up slots from expected PAs through eight innings (0-8 batters). Output: expected runs in top-9 and bottom-9 and P(any run). As-of: lineup post (prior) and live updates. WALK-OFF STOPPING RULE: bottom-9 (and later) runs are computed from a half-inning chain that terminates when the home team takes the lead. Tied entering the bottom: P(any run) = P(chain reaches a go-ahead run), and the run count is 1 unless the final hit is a home run (then 1 + runners on). Home trailing by d: only the first d+1 runs can score, again with the homer exception. This truncated distribution, not the untruncated half-inning run distribution, feeds KXMLBINNINGTOTAL over 1.5 and the Tie strike of KXMLBINNINGWIN.
free_sources: MLB Stats API play-by-play (leverage, pitching changes)

mlb.inning_index_scoring_profile.label: Team scoring and allowed-runs profile by inning index (1st versus 2nd-8th)
mlb.inning_index_scoring_profile.mechanism: Offence is stronger early (top of order due up) and weaker late (relievers, platoon-optimised matchups).
mlb.inning_index_scoring_profile.rationale: League scoring in the first inning exceeds other innings because the best hitters bat; team and park differences in first-inning versus other-inning scoring are mostly noise but have systematic pieces (starter quality, lineup top-heaviness).
mlb.inning_index_scoring_profile.measurement: Per team: runs per half-inning for innings 1, 2-3, 4-6, 7-9 over last 3 seasons, shrink to league-by-inning k = 100 half-innings. Use for baseline; for team-pair adjust multiplicatively by opponent (ratio to league). Units: runs per half-inning. As-of: prior game.

mlb.team_run_correlation_tie_mass.label: Tie probability after nine innings from joint (correlated) run distributions
mlb.team_run_correlation_tie_mass.mechanism: The tie mass depends on the correlation of the two teams' runs through park and weather and on the discrete shapes.
mlb.team_run_correlation_tie_mass.rationale: Independent-NB convolution underestimates ties because shared park/weather effects make both teams' totals move together; high-scoring environments widen the distribution and lower tie mass per run level.
