mlb.team_run_correlation_tie_mass.measurement: Compute P(tie after 9) = sum_k P(R_a=k, R_h=k) from a bivariate NB or copula with correlation rho_park calibrated on 10 seasons of games by park (shrink k = 300 games) and by wind-out indicator; adjust for home team skipping bottom 9 (P(home leads after 8.5) removes some games). Calibrate against observed extras rate by expected-total decile. Units: probability. As-of: lineup post.

mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.label: P(extra innings) from the inning-by-inning score chain, including tie-restoring bottom-9 halves
mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.mechanism: Extras occur whenever the score is level after nine complete innings (or after the home half is played to its end), so the event is a function of the joint inning-by-inning chain, not of a single tied-entering-the-ninth conditional.
mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.rationale: KXMLBEXTRAS pays when at least one extra inning is played. Games reach extras by two routes: tied after the top of the 9th with the home team failing to score, and visitors leading after the top of the 9th with the home team tying the score but not taking the lead (the half-inning ends on the third out, not on the tying run). Modelling only the first route understates P(extras); the home walk-off stopping rule also truncates the bottom-9 run distribution.
mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution.measurement: P(extras) = sum over states s of P(state s entering bottom 9) x P(home half-inning ends with score level), computed from an inning-by-inning Markov chain: states are (run differential after top 9, outs=0) with visitor closer PA rates (shrunk to league reliever rates, k = 150 BF) and home due-up hitters. Tied entering bottom 9: P(level) = P(home scores 0). Home trailing by d>=1: P(level) = P(home scores exactly d runs without taking the lead, the half ends on the third out). Home leading: no bottom 9, P(extras)=0. Walk-off stopping rule applied, so the half-inning ends once the home team takes the lead. Validate on 5 seasons by comparing predicted and observed extras rate by pre-game expected-total decile. Units: probability. As-of: confirmed lineups.

mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.label: Lightning-proximity exposure within the league's 8-mile safety radius over the game window
mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.mechanism: Lightning within a set radius triggers mandatory delays independent of rain amount.
mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.rationale: A forecast of rain probability misses thunderstorms with sparse precipitation; lightning radius rules cause delays even when the field is dry, and conversely rain can come without lightning and be played through.
mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.measurement: From a lightning-strike archive (GOES-R GLM or NLDN), compute historical frequency of strikes within 8 miles of the park during the 3.5-hour window by month and local-hour; combine with the forecast CAPE/convective probability from the forecast vintage via logistic regression calibrated on 5 seasons of recorded delays. Output P(lightning within 8 mi in game window). As-of: 3 hours before first pitch and update at lineup post. Units: probability. ASSUMPTION: the 8-mile radius and 30-minute hold are common convention (stadium or umpire discretion); MLB publishes no uniform league rule. GOES-R GLM gives optical flashes, not NLDN strikes, so archive-based frequencies are a proxy.

mlb.official_delay_record_definition.label: Minimum recorded delay duration and recording rule in official game data
mlb.official_delay_record_definition.mechanism: The contract counts any official weather delay; whether short stoppages are recorded determines what the data can verify.
mlb.official_delay_record_definition.rationale: If delays under about ten minutes are not recorded in the box score or play-by-play, history underestimates the event, and the question of whether a five-minute tarp pause counts is a contract question.
mlb.official_delay_record_definition.measurement: From 5 seasons of MLB Stats API gamefeed and box-score notes: distribution of recorded delay duration; share of games with delay > 10, 30, 60 minutes; compare with weather-station precipitation timing at the park to estimate unrecorded stoppages (rain during play with no delay). Output P(recorded | rain in window) by duration bucket. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for completeness of recording. Units: probability.

mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.label: Crew-specific word and phrase rate per broadcast hour with dispersion (transcript-based)
mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.mechanism: Each crew has a characteristic per-hour rate for each lexeme and a dispersion beyond Poisson.
mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.rationale: The catalog's mention_text names crew language tendencies without a measurement; the question needs per-word per-crew rates and a dispersion estimate because probability of at least one is concave in the rate and depends on clustering.
mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour.measurement: From transcripts (ASR with timestamps) of 40+ games per crew: for each word w count n_gw and exposure hours t_g; fit negative-binomial n_gw ~ NB(mean = t_g * lambda_cw, dispersion phi_cw) with lambda_cw shrunk to national lexeme rate with k = 6 games and phi pooled by word class. Stemming rules follow the contract text version. P(at least one) = 1 - integrated NB zero probability given expected exposure. As-of: before first pitch with crew known.
free_sources: Own ASR transcripts of broadcast audio
Closed captions from MLB.TV or broadcast (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)

mlb.broadcast_airtime_distribution.label: Broadcast airtime distribution (game duration with delay and extras scenarios, plus included pre/post segments)
mlb.broadcast_airtime_distribution.mechanism: Exposure is the time on air, a random variable depending on pace, extras, delays and scheduling.
mlb.broadcast_airtime_distribution.rationale: The mention count scales with airtime, but airtime is uncertain: from a pitch-clock game of 2h25m to a 4h delayed extra-inning game, and pre/post segments may be inside or outside the contract window.
mlb.broadcast_airtime_distribution.measurement: Simulate duration = base minutes (team pair mean time per game, 2023+ pitch-clock regime, half-life 60 games) + 17 minutes x extra innings + delay minutes with probability from delay_risk; shift for pre-game and post-game windows if counted. Output distribution of exposure hours. Shrink team-pair means to league with k = 25 games. As-of: lineup post. Units: hours.

mlb.player_involvement_mention_rate.label: Player and team name mention rate as a function of involvement (PA, pitching, storyline salience)
mlb.player_involvement_mention_rate.mechanism: Names are said when players are in the action or in the news, in proportion to involvement.
mlb.player_involvement_mention_rate.rationale: A market on a specific player's name depends on whether he plays, bats in high-leverage spots, pitches, is injured or traded; base-rate tables for common baseball words do not apply.
mlb.player_involvement_mention_rate.measurement: Model: mentions of player p per game = a_p x (PA_p + BF_p) + b_p x storyline_flag(p) with a_p estimated from 30+ transcribed games shrunk to role-class (star, regular, bench, pitcher) k = 10 games; storyline_flag from news on the previous 3 days (injury return, milestone, award talk). Zero when the player is not active. Units: mentions per game. As-of: lineup post.

mlb.sponsor_read_inventory.label: Scripted sponsor/promo read inventory and tagline language by network
mlb.sponsor_read_inventory.mechanism: Sponsor reads and promos are repeated at fixed cadence and contain fixed vocabulary.
mlb.sponsor_read_inventory.rationale: Words from sponsor segments have near-deterministic rates if the contract counts them; unknown whether they count, but they inflate the rates for brand names and phrases.
mlb.sponsor_read_inventory.measurement: From transcripts: segments classified as sponsor read via keyword templates (for example 'presented by', 'brought to you by'); per-network reads per half-hour and vocabulary, scheduled by network and time. Rate of word w in reads = reads per hour x P(w in read text). Units: occurrences per hour. As-of: network schedule for the date.

mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.label: Manager/executive award score: wins over preseason expectation, division outcome and turnaround
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.mechanism: Awards for managers and executives are voted on surprise and success relative to expectation rather than on absolute record.
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.rationale: Votes correlate more with wins minus preseason projection (and a division title or big turnaround) than with wins alone; the voting ballot closes before the postseason, so late-season trajectory and awards-ballot deadline matter.
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.measurement: score = (actual wins - preseason projected wins, ZiPS/PECOTA/consensus) + 3 x division title flag + 2 x playoff berth + 0.5 x improvement vs prior season wins (scaled), computed at the ballot deadline; map to vote probability by multinomial logit calibrated on 15 seasons of finalist votes (shrink k = 3 seasons). Executive award adds payroll efficiency and offseason acquisitions. Units: composite score and probability. As-of: at ballot deadline and updated daily.

mlb.sale_process_stage_hazard.label: Franchise-sale stage hazard: probability of closing and league approval before a date given process stage
mlb.sale_process_stage_hazard.mechanism: A franchise sale moves through stages with characteristic durations and failure probabilities.
mlb.sale_process_stage_hazard.rationale: Reports of 'agreement in principle' and 'definitive agreement signed' have very different completion odds and timelines; league review and owners' vote add months, and the sampled contract demands finalization and approval before the deadline.
mlb.sale_process_stage_hazard.measurement: Define stages: S0 rumored, S1 exclusive negotiation, S2 signed definitive agreement, S3 under league committee review, S4 owners' vote scheduled, S5 closed. Estimate stage-to-closing completion probability and duration distribution (log-normal or Weibull) from historical MLB sales (small N, about 15 over 20 years) and other major-league franchise sales, with Bayesian shrinkage to cross-league data. P(close before T) = sum over path of stage-duration convolution. As-of: latest credible report timestamp. Units: probability.

mlb.mlbb_team_rating_series_format.label: Mobile Legends team rating (Elo/Glicko) and series-format win probability
mlb.mlbb_team_rating_series_format.mechanism: Match win probability depends on team strength and the best-of format that compresses or amplifies the gap.
mlb.mlbb_team_rating_series_format.rationale: KXMLBBGAME is not baseball; the relevant information is esports team strength, recent roster and patch changes, and map-level results (draft pick and ban), series length (best-of-3 or 5), and regional context.
mlb.mlbb_team_rating_series_format.measurement: Glicko-2 rating per team from map-level results (last 12 months, rating deviation decay), roster-change penalty (reset 30% of rating if >=2 starters change), patch-change variance inflation; match win probability from per-game win probability p and series format: best-of-3 P = p^2(3-2p), best-of-5 P = sum. As-of: at roster lock before the match. Units: probability.

mlb.manager_candidate_selection_signal.label: Manager-hire candidate selection signal: interview reports, candidate pool, internal/external status and executive connections
mlb.manager_candidate_selection_signal.mechanism: Given a vacancy, the hire is a selection among candidates driven by reported interviews, prior relationships with the deciding executive and organizational preference for internal or experienced candidates.
mlb.manager_candidate_selection_signal.rationale: A next-manager market pays per candidate, so identity-level signals matter more than timing or base rates: a reported finalist who worked with the president of baseball operations is far likelier than a name on a speculative list, and reports lead the official announcement.
mlb.manager_candidate_selection_signal.measurement: For each vacancy and candidate record (a) reported interview flag and number of independent outlets reporting it, (b) internal-vs-external flag, (c) years of shared employment with the deciding executive, (d) prior managerial years, (e) days since the vacancy. Fit a conditional-logit selection model over the candidate set on all MLB vacancies 2010-2025 with candidate-level shrinkage (k = 3 vacancies); output selection share per candidate times P(hire announced before the market close). As-of: timestamp of each report; only reports published before the quote time are used.
free_sources: Beat-reporter and national-outlet reports (own timestamped capture)

mlb.late_scratch_hazard.label: Late-scratch hazard between lineup posting and first pitch (conditional on listed starter)
mlb.late_scratch_hazard.mechanism: A posted lineup can still change before the game for illness, injury or warm-up discomfort.
mlb.late_scratch_hazard.rationale: KXMLBSTART resolves No if the player is announced in a lineup and replaced before the game begins; the probability is low on average but elevated for players with day-to-day injuries and for catchers and pitchers.
mlb.late_scratch_hazard.measurement: Over 4 seasons of posted lineups and official starting orders compute P(listed starter not in final starting order) by player injury flag (none, day-to-day, recently returned), position and time between posting and first pitch; logistic with random effect per team (communication practice) shrunk k = 100 games. Output hazard per player-game. As-of: at the lineup posting timestamp. Units: probability. The 1-3% base rate and any start probabilities in the stage text (0.9, 0.3-0.7, 0.1) are illustrative author priors, not fitted values. A separate late-insertion probability (bench player placed in the card before first pitch) is estimated the same way.
free_sources: MLB Stats API lineup changes (historical vintage unverified)

mlb.rehab_progression_stage.label: Rehab progression stage and return-to-pitch/play timeline for injured players
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.mechanism: A returning player must progress through defined rehab steps before appearing, so timing depends on the stage reached.
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.rationale: Window markets such as 'will he pitch before a date' are hazard problems; the information is the rehab stage (throwing program, bullpen sessions, simulated games, minor-league rehab assignment) and the team's stated timetable.
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.measurement: Map each injured player to stages (0 no throwing, 1 long toss, 2 bullpens, 3 simulated/live batting practice, 4 rehab games, 5 activated). Historical stage-to-activation durations by injury type (shoulder, elbow, hamstring) from IL transaction records and rehab-assignment logs; fit survival (Weibull) per injury class with player-age covariates and shrinkage k = 10 players per class. P(pitch in window) = P(activation before window end) x P(used in a game in window | activated). As-of: latest stage report. Units: probability.

mlb.window_exposure_schedule.label: Window exposure: games, off days, doubleheaders and role-probability per game within the window
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.mechanism: A multi-game window aggregates per-game participation probabilities with schedule structure.
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.rationale: P(at least one) in a window depends on the number of team games remaining (off days, doubleheaders, postponement) and on the team's usage pattern; a two-way player's pitching is limited by rotation turns.
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.measurement: N = count of team regular-season games in the window (from schedule; subtract postponements risk). Per-game p_g from the single-game model with rotation slot (for pitchers: number of rotation turns = N/5 rounded). P(at least one) = 1 - Prod(1 - p_g x P(healthy through g)) with injury hazard h per game from injuries_pit. Include end-of-season rest and clinched policy. Units: probability. As-of: daily.

mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.label: Starting-pitcher rotation slot, days of rest, off-day skipping and announced-probable status
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.mechanism: A pitcher starts when his rotation turn arrives after the club's off days, injuries and bullpen days, and when the announced probable is not replaced.
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.rationale: KXMLBSTARTER-type markets depend on the rotation: position in the five-man (or six-man) order, days since the last start, whether the club will skip him around an off day, opener or bullpen-game usage, staff injuries and the probable-pitcher announcement vintage. Hitter lineup-card inputs (platoon, catcher rest, DH rotation) do not describe it.
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.measurement: For each pitcher compute (a) days_rest = game date - last start date, (b) expected next-start date = last start + 5 days adjusted for scheduled off days using the team's last 3 seasons of skip rate on off days (shrunk k = 20 team-off-days), (c) probable-pitcher announcement flag with timestamp and the historical change rate by days-to-game (own capture), (d) opener/bullpen-game rate of the team over the last 30 days. Output P(start on date d) = P(slot lands on d) x P(no change | announced). As-of: announcement time; before announcement the slot-based prior.
free_sources: MLB Stats API schedule hydrate probablePitcher and game logs

mlb.callup_eligibility_pipeline.label: Call-up pipeline: 40-man status, option years, service-time and roster-need signals for a first MLB appearance
mlb.callup_eligibility_pipeline.mechanism: A debut requires 40-man roster addition, a roster vacancy or injury need, and a club decision informed by prospect readiness and service-time incentives.
mlb.callup_eligibility_pipeline.rationale: KXMLBDEBUT cannot be modelled by lineup inputs: it depends on whether the player is on the 40-man, whether a need exists at his position, the club's service-time and Rule 5/waiver considerations, minor-league performance and September roster rules. The date of the market window determines which of these dominates.
mlb.callup_eligibility_pipeline.measurement: Features per prospect: on-40-man flag, option years remaining, MiLB level and age-relative OPS/ERA over the last 120 PA/IP, position-need score = 1 - depth-chart strength at the MLB position, injury count at the position, days to window end, and service-time-manipulation flag (days needed to avoid an extra year). Fit a discrete-time hazard of debut per day on 2015-2025 call-ups with prospect-level shrinkage (k = 5 promotions per team-year). Output P(debut before date). As-of: daily.
free_sources: MLB Stats API transactions and rosters

mlb.contract_status_and_service_clock.label: Contract status and service clock (expiry, options, opt-outs, no-trade, qualifying-offer eligibility)
mlb.contract_status_and_service_clock.mechanism: Transactions are possible only when contractual and CBA conditions allow them.
mlb.contract_status_and_service_clock.rationale: A player's free-agency status, club or player option, no-trade protection, arbitration status and service time determine the set and timing of feasible events; 'next team' markets differ sharply for players under contract versus free agents.
mlb.contract_status_and_service_clock.measurement: Per player: contract end year, options (club/player/mutual with decision dates), opt-out dates, no-trade clause, 10-5 rights, arbitration years, qualifying-offer eligibility (service with one team, prior QO), service-time days at date. Output eligibility flags and dates. As-of: latest public contract data. Units: flags and dates.

mlb.news_source_reliability_score.label: Source-level reliability: P(official | report type) from historical reports
mlb.news_source_reliability_score.mechanism: Not all reports are equal; some reporters' 'agreement reached' items are nearly always followed by official moves.
mlb.news_source_reliability_score.rationale: Market reaction to reports is only warranted if the posterior given the source and wording exceeds the market's pricing; track record and wording ('close', 'agreed', 'pending physical') strongly change completion probability.
mlb.news_source_reliability_score.measurement: For each reporter-source and wording class compute historical fraction of reports that led to the official event within 14 days (Beta posterior with prior from class average, k = 10 reports) and distribution of lead time. Output P(official by date) and expected lead. As-of: report timestamp. Units: probability and days.
free_sources: social media archives (unavailable_public via API limits)

mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.label: Calendar hazard function by transaction type (trade, free-agent signing, extension, manager hire)
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.mechanism: Hazard of each event type is concentrated on known dates.
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.rationale: Using a flat per-day rate misprices markets that straddle deadlines and meeting dates; for example, a large share of free-agent signings occur in specific off-season windows and trade completions spike near the deadline.
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.measurement: From 15 years of transactions: daily event counts per type normalized by eligible stock; fit a piecewise log-linear hazard with calendar-anchor dummies (deadline week, winter meetings week, non-tender day, spring training start). Output h(d) for the window dates and survival to the end. Shrink per-type to pooled with k = 3 seasons. Units: events per eligible per day. As-of: current stock of eligible players.

mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.label: Competitive-balance-tax and payroll headroom for the acquiring team
mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.mechanism: Finance constrains who can absorb salary.
mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.rationale: Teams near luxury-tax thresholds or with stated payroll limits are much less likely to add salary; headroom also determines trade behaviour.
mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.measurement: Headroom = CBT threshold - projected CBT payroll (average annual value of contracts for 40-man roster + benefits) for the team at the date; flags for crossing the first/second threshold; share of owner-stated budget. Units: dollars and flag. As-of: latest transaction.

mlb.manager_firing_hazard.label: Manager seat heat: tenure, underperformance vs expectation, contract expiry and owner statements
mlb.manager_firing_hazard.mechanism: Managers are removed when results fall short of expectations and the owner or front office is willing to act.
mlb.manager_firing_hazard.rationale: Next-manager markets resolve on a hiring event preceded by a vacancy; the vacancy hazard depends on wins below projection, contract status, front-office change and public statements.
mlb.manager_firing_hazard.measurement: Hazard = logistic on (wins - preseason projected wins) per 162, tenure years, contract years remaining (<=1 flag), prior-year playoff flag, recent front-office change, and winning percentage trailing 30 games; calibrate on 20 years of mid-season and off-season manager changes (shrink k = 3 seasons). Units: probability of vacancy before date. As-of: current day.

mlb.destination_selection_signal.label: Destination or candidate selection signal: positional need, competing bidders, market size, player preference and qualifying-offer status (players); interview pool and executive connections (managers)
mlb.destination_selection_signal.mechanism: KXMLBNEXTTEAM and KXMLBCOACH resolve one market per team or candidate, so the outcome is a categorical choice, not just whether a transaction occurs.
mlb.destination_selection_signal.rationale: Eligibility and timing hazards say when a move happens but not where: the signing team depends on roster need at the player's position, who can afford him, market size and ownership spending, the player's stated preferences or hometown ties, whether his old team made a qualifying offer, and for managers the interview pool and ties to the decision maker. The existing payroll-headroom input does not carry competing bids.
mlb.destination_selection_signal.measurement: For each free agent compute for every team t: need_t = 1 - projected WAR share of the incumbent at his position (ZiPS depth charts), afford_t = projected payroll headroom below the tax line scaled by the contract's AAV, reported_interest_t = count of independent timestamped outlets naming t (own capture) with shrinkage k = 2 reports, market_t = indicator of top-10 market revenue, and prior_team_t flag with qualifying-offer flag. Fit a conditional-logit destination model on FA classes 2012-2025 (team-level fixed effects shrunk, k = 3 signings). For managers use the interview-report and executive-tie features in the vacancy table. Output P(destination = t | signs before date). As-of: report timestamps.

mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.label: Labour-stoppage regime: CBA expiry (Dec 1 2026), lockout flag and expected end, and transaction freeze rules
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.mechanism: A lockout freezes 40-man roster transactions and free-agent signings, turning a window into a pre-expiry rush, a frozen interval of unknown length and a post-deal rush.
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.rationale: The 2022 CBA expires at 11:59 pm ET on Dec 1 2026 and a lockout is widely reported as likely; in 2021-22 the lockout froze 40-man transactions from Dec 2 until Mar 10 2022. A next-team market closing Mar 25 2027 and any call-up or opening-day contract in 2027 are therefore mixtures over stoppage length, and 15 years of calendar hazard history include only one such stoppage.
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.measurement: State variables: days to CBA expiry, lockout flag, days since lockout start, reported negotiation status (own capture of timestamped reports coded into ordinal stage 0-4). Model the stoppage length L with a survival model whose prior is built from the 1994-95, 2021-22 and 1990 stoppages (3 events, heavy shrinkage) and updated by negotiation stage; apply the freeze: hazard of any 40-man transaction = 0 during lockout, with a post-agreement rush multiple estimated from March 2022 (units: multiple of baseline hazard). Output P(freeze covers date d) and the adjusted calendar hazard. As-of: daily.

mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.label: Team talent posterior (mean and standard deviation) combining projection prior and run differential
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.mechanism: True team strength is uncertain; its spread determines the width of win-total and title distributions.
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.rationale: A single rating hides that April uncertainty is large and that roster shocks widen it; futures prices at tails (95+ wins, a long-shot pennant) depend on the variance more than the mean.
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.measurement: Prior mean mu0 = preseason projected win% (average of ZiPS/Steamer/PECOTA) with prior sd s0 = 0.04. Data: pythagenpat win% from RS/RA with n games and per-game outcome variance s_game^2 = 0.25 (binomial; use 0.22 for run-based). Conjugate normal update: weight on data w = n/(n + k) with k = s_game^2 / s0^2 = 0.25/0.0016 = about 156 games, so posterior mean = (1-w) mu0 + w pyth_wp and posterior variance = 1/(1/s0^2 + n/s_game^2); at n = 140 this gives sd of about 0.029 and at n = 162 about 0.028. Add roster shock: change in rest-of-season projected WAR per 162 games divided by 162 added to the mean, with variance 0.002 per shock. Units: win probability per game. As-of: daily after games.

mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.label: Tiebreaker state (head-to-head and divisional records) and seed-to-bracket path matrix
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.mechanism: Ties in win totals are broken by specified records, and seed determines opponents and home field in a known bracket.
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.rationale: Close races resolve through head-to-head records, not just wins; markets on seeds and qualifiers depend on tiebreakers, which are fully determined by games already played and remaining head-to-head games.
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.measurement: For each pair of contenders compute current head-to-head wins/losses, remaining head-to-head games, intradivision records and the next criteria in the official tiebreaker order (head-to-head, intradivision, intraleague, last-half record); in simulation resolve ties by those criteria from simulated game outcomes. Path matrix: seed 1-6 per league mapped to round-1 opponent, bye, home-field for each round (12-team format). Output P(seed s), P(path). As-of: daily.
free_sources: MLB standings and tiebreaker rules documentation

mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.label: Playoff-adjusted team rating (top-3 starters, top relievers, regular lineup) for short series
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.mechanism: In October rotations shorten and top relievers pitch more, so the relevant team strength differs from the regular-season average.
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.rationale: A team's regular-season run differential includes innings from fourth and fifth starters and mid bullpen arms that disappear in the playoffs; the weights shift toward the top of the rotation, top bullpen arms and starting lineup.
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.measurement: Rating = lineup wRC+ of the expected playoff nine (position players >= 70% of PA) + weights on top-3 starters (about 0.6 of innings in a series) using projection runs per 9 + top-4 relievers weights (about 0.3 of bullpen innings) minus bench contribution. Compute run differential per game with these weights vs the opponent; map to per-game win probability by logistic (0.1 per run). As-of: playoff roster and announced rotation. Units: expected run difference per game.

mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.label: Deadline roster strength shift (net rest-of-season WAR added/lost via trades and call-ups)
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.mechanism: Teams change materially at the trade deadline; sellers lose talent, buyers add it.
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.rationale: Win-total futures after the deadline need a changed mean; a team that sells a star shifts its remaining win rate down by a measurable amount, which the season-to-date record does not reflect.
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.measurement: For each transaction after date d: delta_WAR_rest = projected rest-of-season WAR of players acquired minus those traded away (ROS projections by FanGraphs/ZiPS), per 162 -> converted to win probability per game: delta_p = delta_WAR_rest / games_remaining. Sum over team transactions. Include IL return and call-up adjustments. Units: win probability per game. As-of: transaction date.

mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.label: Season state: wins, losses, games remaining, run differential to date and ties/suspended games
mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.mechanism: A win-total threshold is wins already banked plus the number of wins in the remaining games, so the state variables set how much uncertainty is left.
mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.rationale: The primary state of a win-total ladder is not a rating but how many wins are banked and how many games remain; the required additional wins W_needed = N - wins and the remaining games determine the binomial tail, and the posterior from run differential only prices the per-game probability. Suspended or cancelled games change games remaining.
mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.measurement: Daily from standings: W, L, G_rem = 162 - W - L (adjusted for suspended or cancelled games per the official schedule), W_needed = N - W, run differential RD and pythagenpat win% to date. P(wins >= N) = sum over k >= W_needed of P(Bin-mixture(G_rem, p_i)) where p_i is the per-game probability from the talent posterior. Units: wins and games. As-of: after each day's final games.

mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.label: Postseason bracket-path enumeration: pairing, series length and home-field pattern probabilities
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.mechanism: Matchup, games-hosted and qualifier contracts are functions of which teams reach which round and how long each series lasts.
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.rationale: KXMLBMATCHUP and KXMLBPLAYOFFHOST resolve on bracket pairing and on how many games each team hosts, which requires enumerating the fixed bracket (no reseeding within the 12-team format, to be verified) with series-length distributions and home-field patterns, not a title-probability number.
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.measurement: Enumerate all bracket paths from the current seeds or seed probabilities: P(path) = product of series-win probabilities from the team-strength posterior; series length distribution from per-game probabilities with home-field pattern (2-3-2 or 2-2-1-1-1) and shared team-strength draws; games hosted = sum over series of the home games in the realised length. Output P(matchup A vs B in round r) and the distribution of games hosted by a team. As-of: daily.

mlb.series_mvp_credit_share.label: Series and World Series MVP: P(team wins series) times a player credit-share model
mlb.series_mvp_credit_share.mechanism: Series MVP is chosen from the winning team, so probability = P(team wins) times the player's share of the winning team's credit, which depends on his series performance and star status.
mlb.series_mvp_credit_share.rationale: KXMLBWSMVP and the championship-series MVP markets pay on the official named winner (co-winners $1/N). The winner comes from the winning team, with voters rewarding series-leading production and narrative; a team's win probability alone overstates its weaker contributors.
mlb.series_mvp_credit_share.measurement: P(player MVP) = P(his team wins series) x share_i where share_i = softmax over his team's players of (a x series WPA/RE24 to date + b x pre-series star score (3-season WAR, shrunk k = 3 series)), fitted on MVP voting 2000-2025 series with a pooled coefficient; co-winner probability from history. As-of: after each game for in-series updating. Units: probability.

mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.label: Playoff games played and plate-appearance distribution for a named player (for playoff-leader markets)
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.mechanism: A playoff statistical leader needs games played, which depends on the team's bracket survival, and PA per game, which depends on lineup slot.
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.rationale: KXMLBLEADERPLAYOFF counts only playoff statistics and resolves No for non-participants, so the leader distribution is a maximum over players of a count over a random number of games; the games-played distribution comes from bracket survival and the PA share from lineup slot and rest.
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.measurement: For each candidate: G_i = games in his team's remaining path from the bracket enumeration (distribution), PA per game by slot (4.3-4.6 for slots 1-3 falling to about 3.9), start probability from the lineup model; per-PA rate shrunk to projection (k = 300 PA). Simulate the stat count for each candidate over G_i and take the maximum; ties split per the contract. Output P(leader). As-of: daily.

mlb.award_vote_rank_model.label: Rank-ordered voter model (Plackett-Luce) for award points and finalists
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.mechanism: Awards are decided by ballots ranking candidates; the distribution over rankings, not a single score, gives winner and finalist probabilities.
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.rationale: A winner market and a finalist market need different parts of the same ranking distribution; point totals depend on ballot structure (first-place votes, 10-deep ballots) and on how the voters weigh WAR, counting stats and team success.
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.measurement: Fit Plackett-Luce on 15 seasons of MVP/Cy Young/ROY ballot results: utility_i = b1*WAR_z + b2*team_success + b3*counting_stat_z + b4*narrative_flag + position effects; voter-level noise variance estimated from vote dispersion; shrink coefficients across awards with k = 3 seasons. For finalist market compute P(rank <= 3) by simulation with voter noise. As-of: ballot deadline stats plus narrative flags. Units: probabilities.

mlb.roy_eligibility_status.label: Rookie-of-the-Year eligibility status and candidate set (rookie limits on at-bats, innings and active-roster days)
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.mechanism: ROY eligibility depends on prior at-bats, innings pitched and days on the active roster; some prominent players are ineligible.
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.rationale: A market on a prominent debutant must be restricted to eligible candidates; mistaking an ineligible player for a contender mis-sets the field, and call-up timing affects total production.
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.measurement: For each player compute career MLB at-bats, innings pitched and days on the active roster (excluding time on the injured list; the former September-expansion exemption is not assumed to apply with fixed rosters, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) before the season; eligible if at-bats <= 130 and innings <= 50 and days <= 45 (thresholds stated as commonly cited, not verified as the current rule; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for 2026). Output eligibility flag and the set of prospects with call-up probability (MLB Pipeline rankings, 40-man status). Units: flag and probability. As-of: day.

mlb.award_timing_information_state.label: Award calendar information state (ballot deadline, finalist announcement date, announcement-before-winner condition)
mlb.award_timing_information_state.mechanism: Awards have a fixed calendar: ballots close before the postseason, finalists are announced, then winners.
mlb.award_timing_information_state.rationale: The finalist contract resolves No if finalists are not announced before the winner, and finalist announcements are information events that collapse winner uncertainty; knowing which dates are fixed and which are not is part of settlement.
mlb.award_timing_information_state.measurement: Table by award and season: ballot deadline, finalist announcement date, winner date, announcing agency; compute historical lag between finalist and winner announcements (days) and the fraction of awards with a finalist announcement at all (by award type). P(finalists announced before winner) from that history (Beta prior, k = 5 seasons). Units: dates and probability. As-of: current season calendar.

mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.label: Monthly/weekly window production rank (OPS, HR, ERA, K) within the award window
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.mechanism: Player of the Month/Week is chosen from production over a short window by a selection committee.
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.rationale: Short windows are noisy and the top performer in OPS or ERA is largely determined by luck, but the selection rule (batters from each league, pitchers separately) and narrative create structure.
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.measurement: Rank players by composite score = z(wOBA or xwOBA) + z(HR) for hitters; z(ERA-) + z(K) for pitchers over the window (min PA/IP), using the final days before the selection date. Probability of selection from a logistic calibrated on 10 years of selection outcomes with features rank, team playoff odds, repeat winners. Units: probability. As-of: window end.

mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.label: Triple Crown joint leader probability (batting average, home runs, RBI) with correlations
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.mechanism: Triple Crown requires leading all three categories; they are positively correlated but the batting-average race has qualification and different drivers.
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.rationale: Product of marginal leader probabilities overstates the event if categories were independent and understates it if highly correlated; the joint distribution matters.
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.measurement: Simulate final totals for all qualifying contenders using rest-of-season projections (HR, RBI, AVG) with correlation structure among stats (HR-RBI and AVG-HR correlations are illustrative author guesses, to be estimated, not cited values) estimated from 20 seasons of player-season data; apply qualification (3.1 PA per team game) for AVG; P = probability one player leads all three (ties handling per contract). Units: probability. As-of: daily.

mlb.all_star_selection_model.label: All-Star selection model: fan-vote phases, player vote, commissioner/roster-fill rules and positional slots
mlb.all_star_selection_model.mechanism: A player is selected through fan voting that fixes starters, a player vote and then commissioner or roster-fill picks, so selection probability depends on vote share, position slot and team-representation rules.
mlb.all_star_selection_model.rationale: KXMLBALLSTAR cannot be modelled from season production alone: starters are fan-determined, reserves player-chosen and pitchers and replacements follow rules, with injured selectees replaced and each team is assured a representative.
mlb.all_star_selection_model.measurement: P(selected) = P(starter via fan vote) + P(reserve via player vote | not starter) + P(added by commissioner or as replacement | neither). Fan-vote share modelled from last-year vote share, WAR rank at the ballot-close date and market size with a multinomial logit by position (shrinkage k = 2 seasons); player-vote probability from WAR rank within position; team-representation fill from the rule that each club has at least one selectee. Calibrate on 2015-2025 selections. As-of: ballot phase timestamps.

mlb.all_star_game_event_model.label: All-Star Game result and MVP model: league talent, exhibition usage and MVP credit given the winning team
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.mechanism: The exhibition has equal-stakes, short-stint pitcher usage and substitution rules, so the result is close to a coin flip and the MVP comes from the winning team's players with the most plate appearances and highlights.
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.rationale: KXMLBASGAME and KXMLBASGMVP resolve on a one-off game: league strength differences are tiny relative to variance, and MVP depends on the winning side, plate appearances and extra-base or home-run events.
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.measurement: P(league wins) from the difference in selected-roster strength (summed projected wOBA/ERA by lineup and pitching slots) mapped through the game-win logistic with a compressed slope (about 0.5 of the regular-season slope, to be estimated from 2010-2025 results). P(MVP = player) = P(his league wins) x share, share = softmax of expected plate appearances x per-PA highlight probability (HR, multi-hit) with a pitcher-specific term for the winning pitcher. As-of: roster announcement and starting lineups.

mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.label: Draft lottery odds by prior-season record and eligibility rules
mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.mechanism: Draft position is set by a lottery among non-playoff clubs whose odds are fixed by prior-season record, with restrictions on consecutive top-pick wins.
mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.rationale: KXMLBDRAFTPICK is not an award or race: the probability of a given pick is a lottery function of record rank, the number of lottery slots and the consecutive-win restrictions.
mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.measurement: Odds table P(pick = j | record rank r) from the official lottery rules (non-playoff clubs, odds by reverse record rank, lottery covering the first picks, restrictions on repeated winners and revenue-sharing recipients), with record ranks from the final standings and tiebreaker; simulate the lottery. Units: probability by pick slot. As-of: final standings. The numeric odds table for the draft in question is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED here.

mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.label: Joint distribution of award outcomes for combination markets
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.mechanism: A combination market pays only if several awards go to specified outcomes, whose probabilities are correlated through shared player performance and team narrative.
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.rationale: KXMLBAWARDCOMBO needs P(A and B), not the product: an MVP and Cy Young from the same team are positively dependent via team success, while two MVPs in different leagues are nearly independent; the electorates also differ.
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.measurement: Estimate pairwise dependence between award outcomes by a Gaussian copula fitted to 25 seasons of winners (same-team indicator, shared-electorate indicator) shrunk to independence with k = 10 seasons; P(A and B) = C(P(A), P(B); rho). Units: probability. As-of: after finalists are announced.

mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.label: League order-statistic engine for best/worst record, 100+ losses, longest losing streak and team strikeouts (simulation method; its inputs are mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_vintage)
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.mechanism: The extreme among thirty teams is determined by each team's talent distribution and the shared schedule.
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.rationale: Existing inputs address single games; extremes require a league-wide simulation where each team's outcome is drawn jointly, ties are tracked for $1/N payouts, and streak and strikeout statistics are computed from game-level sequences.
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.measurement: Simulate remaining games for 30 teams using team talent posterior (mean, sd) and schedule; record final wins, the longest loss streak per team (run-length of simulated sequence) and team strikeouts (batters faced x team K rate with pitching staff K% projection, sd from game-level variance). Outputs: P(team is unique best), P(tied for best with N teams), expected payout with $1/N rounding; P(wins <= 62 for 100 losses). 20k simulations; calibrate sd to historical. As-of: daily. Units: probabilities.

mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.label: Joint season HR-SB distribution for one hitter (power-speed profile, PA, availability)
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.mechanism: A 50 HR and 40 SB season is a joint tail of two correlated counts requiring health and PA.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.rationale: The probability depends on the hitter's season-to-date pace, remaining PA and the rates of both events, and the two are correlated through playing time and hitter quality; independence misprices.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.measurement: Given current HR, SB and remaining games: HR_rest ~ NB with mean = rate_HR * PA_rest, SB_rest ~ NB with mean = rate_SB * PA_rest x opportunity; PA_rest from games remaining x P(play) x PA per game; correlation via shared PA factor and a latent role; compute P(HR >= 50 and SB >= 40) by simulation. Rates from rest-of-season projection blended with current-season pace (shrunk k = 250 PA). Units: probability. As-of: daily.

mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.label: Extreme pitch-speed distribution (probability of a 107+ mph pitch given pitcher max velocities and pitch counts)
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.mechanism: The fastest pitch of a season is the maximum over pitches of a speed distribution with a heavy upper tail for a few pitchers.
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.rationale: A threshold of 107.0 mph is at the edge of the known distribution; the probability depends on a handful of pitchers' maximum fastball velocities, their usage and number of high-velocity pitches, and the tracking system measuring release speed.
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.measurement: For each pitcher: fit a generalized extreme value (GEV) or exponential tail to the pitcher's fastball speeds (top 1% of pitches) using the last 2 seasons; expected number of fastballs in the remaining window N_i; P(max_i >= 107) = 1 - exp(-N_i * P(speed >= 107 | fastball)). Combine across pitchers P(any) = 1 - Prod(1 - p_i). Include postseason pitches only for playoff teams. Units: probability. As-of: daily, with current-season maximum. CAVEATS: 107 mph lies beyond the observed record (about 105-106 mph tracked, unverified here), so an exponential tail fitted to the top 1% extrapolates; a physical-ceiling cap or generalised-Pareto fit with a finite endpoint is required. Independence across pitchers in P(any) = 1 - prod(1 - p_i) is an assumption (shared parks, radar calibration).

mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.label: Series exact score distribution (4-0, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3 for each team) from game win probabilities with dependence
mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.mechanism: Exact series scores follow from the sequence of game outcomes and the best-of format.
mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.rationale: Each score has a different probability and depends on home-field pattern, starters and dependence between games; independent games underpricing sweeps and seven-game series.
mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.measurement: Simulate series with game probabilities p_i from starter-specific model; shared strength offset N(0, 0.04); stop at four wins; compute probabilities of the eight exact scores. Home pattern 2-2-1-1-1 or 2-3-2 as applicable. Calibrate offset sd on best-of-seven history since 2012. As-of: after each game. Units: probabilities.

mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.label: Longest winning streak: extreme-value distribution given team win probabilities and remaining games
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.mechanism: The longest win streak across teams is the maximum over runs of consecutive wins; the season-level maximum is an extreme value.
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.rationale: Season streak markets are filed in this archetype but are not inning markets; the winning team is the one with the longest run, with ties paying $1/N, so the exact distribution of the maximum run for each team (given per-game win probability, mostly 0.4-0.65) determines the odds.
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.measurement: For team i with games remaining n_i, current streak c_i and per-game win prob p_ij: P(longest streak >= L) computed by a run-length Markov chain; account for heterogeneity of p_ij by opponent and home/away, and current maximum across league to date. P(team has strict maximum) = Prod over rivals (1 - ...) with Monte Carlo and tie share 1/N (payout rounded down). Streak serial correlation assumed zero unless tested. As-of: daily. Units: probability. Postponed, suspended and cancelled games are excluded from the sequence; the streak model assumes independent games conditional on p_ij, so serial correlation and doubleheader order are assumptions.

mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.label: Lockout and shortened-season scenario: P(lockout), start/end dates and games lost under each scenario
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.mechanism: A CBA lockout after Dec 1 2026 could delay opening day and cancel games, so season-games and opening-day outcomes are mixtures over scenarios.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.rationale: A 600-game strike equals roughly a quarter of the 2,430-game schedule and a May 31 opening cutoff is a long delay; both are plausible stoppage thresholds. In 2021-22 the lockout postponed opening day by about one week with no games lost (to my knowledge), but 1994-95 lost the end of one season and the start of the next; the distribution of games lost is heavy-tailed with a large mass at zero.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.measurement: Scenario mixture: P(no lockout) from negotiation state (own timestamped coding of reports, ordinal 0-4); conditional on a lockout, the stoppage end date drawn from a survival model with prior from 1990, 1994-95 and 2021-22 (3 events, strongly shrunk) updated by negotiation stage; games lost = schedule games before the agreed start date after a compressed ramp-up (about 3 weeks of spring training), with doubleheaders making up part. Output: P(first regular-season game before May 31 2027) and P(games played > 600) = P(games lost < 1,830). As-of: daily.

mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.label: All-30-team talent posteriors with projection vintage, remaining schedule and head-to-head structure
mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.mechanism: League-wide order statistics need every team's win-probability distribution, correlated through the shared schedule.
mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.rationale: Best record, worst record, 100+ losses and the longest-streak markets are maxima over 30 teams; the engine inputs are the 30 posterior means and sds, the remaining schedule and projection vintages, not the engine itself.
mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.measurement: For each team i: posterior mean p_i and sd s_i from preseason projection (average of ZiPS/Steamer, prior sd 0.04) updated by pythagenpat win% with conjugate normal weights (k = s_game^2/s0^2 about 156 games), as-of daily; remaining schedule with opponent posteriors and home flags; projection vintage stored at each date so backtests use only information available then. Output: 30 x (p_i, s_i), the 30-team opponent matrix and remaining games. As-of: after each day's games.

game_side.target: Which team wins the game (and by how many runs for spread/margin contracts), settled after the final out including extra innings unless the wording says otherwise.
game_side.mechanism: Win probability follows from the expected run difference: starter run prevention for the innings he works, bullpen quality for the rest, lineup quality against the specific starter's handedness and arsenal, and park/weather/umpire scaling of both offences. Home field adds a small edge. Because late information (confirmed lineups, scratched starter, weather) moves the line, the model's value comes from timely incorporation and from regressing luck-heavy team results; margin and spread contracts additionally need the run-difference distribution including extra-innings tie breaking.

interactions.hypothesis: Starter quality only matters for the innings he pitches, so starter edge should be weighted by expected batters faced and the quality gap to the bullpen that replaces him.
Lineup handedness against starter handedness: a platoon-weak confirmed lineup lowers team strength more than season-level wRC+ suggests, so team offence should be lineup-by-hand specific.
Wind and park interact: wind-out adds more runs in HR-friendly parks and for fly-ball pitchers, so the effect should be multiplied with park HR factor and pitcher fly-ball rate.

game_total.target: Total runs (or one team's runs) in the game, with the contract defining whether extra-innings runs count and how shortened games settle.
game_total.mechanism: Expected runs are the sum over plate appearances of per-PA run value, determined by starter quality for the early innings, bullpen quality for the late innings, the lineups' quality by handedness, park and weather (air density, wind), and the umpire's zone. Run distributions are overdispersed and clustered by inning, so threshold prices depend on dispersion and not just the mean; late-breaking information (confirmed lineups, wind, roof status, scratched starters) is the main source of mispricing.

player_hit.target: Hitter counting outcomes in a game: hits, total bases, RBIs, runs or stolen bases (threshold ladders), requiring the player to appear per the wording.
player_hit.mechanism: Each count is the sum over the hitter's plate appearances of per-PA outcome probabilities, so expected value = expected PA (lineup slot, team scoring, substitution risk) x per-PA rates (contact quality, K/BB, platoon, pitch-type matchup, park, weather, defence) with the opposing starter's quality for the first two or three PAs and the bullpen for the rest. RBI, runs and SB additionally depend on teammates' on-base and the situation, making them more variable and less skill-pure.

Starter exit probability before the fifth is the major structural uncertainty and ties are possible, so rules matter (push vs loss).

interactions.hypothesis: Pitch cap x pitches per out: the ceiling on outs is cap divided by pitches per out, so the cap and efficiency (and opponent patience) interact and determine the upper tail.
Performance-triggered hook: early runs and baserunners trigger pulls, so run-prevention quality, contact allowed and manager hook policy interact to create the left tail of outs.
Bullpen state x leash: a depleted bullpen lengthens the starter's leash while a rested bullpen and analytics-driven manager shorten it before the third trip.
Opener flag x listed pitcher: opener usage collapses outs (and may void), so probable-pitcher status must gate every other input.

pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks.label: Starting pitcher earned runs, hits allowed and walks allowed
pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks.target: Whether the starter allows at least k earned runs, hits or walks in the game, requiring the pitcher to start per the wording.
pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks.mechanism: All three are batters faced times a per-PA event rate, but with different structure: hits depend on contact quality, defence and BABIP luck with K and BB removing balls in play; walks depend on the pitcher's command versus the lineup's patience and on the umpire zone and framing; earned runs add sequencing (LOB%, HR) on top of baserunners and truncate with the hook. The three are positively correlated within a start through shared latent command and contact quality and negatively with outs/strikeouts. Luck components (BABIP, LOB%, HR/FB) are large and regress, so expected-rate models beat observed outcomes.

interactions.hypothesis: Hits = balls in play x hit rate: K% and BB% determine balls in play, contact quality and defence determine conversion, so strikeout and contact profiles must be combined, not treated as independent.

Earned-run tail: HR vulnerability x park/wind x hook; early HR-driven blow-ups cause pulls, truncating but fattening the middle of the distribution.
Luck regression: observed BABIP and LOB% revert, so expected hits and earned runs use xBABIP and FIP-style run estimators with sample-weighted shrinkage.

hitter_hits_and_total_bases.label: Hitter hits, total bases and hits+runs+RBIs thresholds
hitter_hits_and_total_bases.target: Whether a hitter records at least k hits, total bases or H+R+RBI in the game, requiring appearance per the wording.
hitter_hits_and_total_bases.mechanism: Hits and total bases are sums over plate appearances of per-PA outcome probabilities (single, double, triple, HR vs out), so the expected value is expected PAs (lineup slot, team scoring, substitution risk) times per-PA rates and the distribution is a compound binomial/multinomial. Per-PA rates combine the hitter's contact quality, K and BB, platoon, pitch-type matchup against the starter, park and weather, defence, and later the bullpen; BABIP luck regresses. H+R+RBI adds team-dependent components (runners ahead, hitters behind), increasing variance and correlation with team scoring.

interactions.hypothesis: PA count x per-PA probability: expected hits = expected PA x P(hit per PA); the lineup slot and team total shift PA while contact quality shifts probability, so both must be in one compound model.
Platoon x pitch-type matchup: same-handed breaking-ball-heavy starters suppress hitters with weak breaking-ball performance, so platoon and pitch-mix effects interact rather than add.
Contact quality x defence/park: expected TB depends on how hard and where a hitter hits the ball relative to park dimensions and fielders, so xSLG should be park- and defence-adjusted.
BABIP luck x recent form: recent hot hitting driven by BABIP should not move the projection, so recent form should enter through contact quality, not batting average.

hitter_home_runs.label: Hitter home runs (1+ / 2+)
hitter_home_runs.target: Whether a hitter hits at least one (or two) home runs in the game, requiring appearance per the wording.
hitter_home_runs.mechanism: HR per game = 1 - product over PAs of (1 - p_HR), where per-PA HR probability multiplies the hitter's fly-ball/pull/barrel profile by the pitcher's HR vulnerability (by handedness and pitch type), the park's handedness-specific HR factor and the weather (wind component, temperature/air density). Because the base probability is low, multiplicative environment shifts matter and the dominant uncertainty is Bernoulli luck; HR/FB regresses to a contact-quality-determined mean. PA count (batting slot) and the bullpen's HR vulnerability also matter.

Per-PA home-run probability, compounded over expected PAs, gives the any-HR probability; park, wind and pitcher enter per PA.

Connects hitter spray profile to day-specific carry, a more exact form of the park-by-wind interaction than separate factors.

interactions.hypothesis: Hitter pull-air profile x park pull-side HR factor x wind: HR probability depends on the hitter's spray direction relative to the park's short side and the wind along that line, so the three should be modelled jointly.
Barrel rate x pitcher HR vulnerability x pitch type: HR risk is highest when a hitter's strong pitch type meets a pitcher who throws it in the damage zone, so matchup is by pitch type and zone.
Air density x wind x park: warm, thin air plus out-blowing wind in a short-porch park compound, but are already partially included in park factors, so use deviation from park norms.
PA count x per-PA HR rate: because per-PA HR probability is small, extra PA from batting slot or team scoring matters almost linearly, interacting with lineup posting and substitution risk.

hitter_rbis_runs_sb.label: Hitter RBIs, runs scored and stolen bases
hitter_rbis_runs_sb.target: Whether a hitter records at least k RBIs or stolen bases in the game (runs and combos via H+R+RBI are in the hits archetype), requiring appearance per the wording.
hitter_rbis_runs_sb.mechanism: RBI depend on the number of runners on base when the hitter bats (OBP of hitters ahead, team scoring) and the hitter's ability to drive them in (power, contact, situational), so they are heavily context-dependent and high-variance, with lineup slot and team total dominating. Stolen bases require reaching base, deciding to attempt (runner speed, manager, game state) and succeeding against the pitcher's hold time and the catcher's arm, a low-frequency event with rule-regime shifts (pickoff limits, bigger bases). Both markets depend on lineup confirmation and on the opposing starter and catcher.

SB attempt: runner speed x pitcher hold time x catcher arm x game state; each factor changes both attempt and success and they must be combined (a slow pitcher with a weak catcher invites attempts by fast runners).

game_moneyline.label: Game winner, run line and winning margin
game_moneyline.target: Which team wins the game (including extra innings unless worded otherwise), covers a run spread, or wins by a particular margin.
game_moneyline.mechanism: Win probability is built from expected run scoring and prevention for each team at the plate-appearance level: starter quality and expected innings, bullpen quality and availability, confirmed lineup quality against the starter's hand and arsenal, defence, park and weather and the umpire's zone, with a modest home-field effect. The win probability is a function of the run-difference distribution (overdispersed, with extra-innings resolution of ties), so run line and margin contracts need the full distribution rather than the moneyline alone. Late information (confirmed lineups, scratched starters, weather/roof) is the main edge source, and records must be regressed to run-based talent.

game_total_and_team_total.label: Game total and team total runs
game_total_and_team_total.target: Whether total runs (or one team's runs) exceed a threshold under the contract's scope (including extra innings, shortened game rules).
game_total_and_team_total.mechanism: Expected runs = sum over plate appearances of per-PA run value for each team, driven by starter quality over the innings he pitches, bullpen run rate for the rest, the lineups' quality by handedness, and multiplicative park/weather/air-density and umpire effects; the realised distribution is overdispersed and inning-clustered so thresholds price tail probabilities. Team totals isolate one offence against the opposing pitching staff and defence. The main edges are late environmental/lineup information (wind, roof, confirmed lineup, scratched starter) and correct dispersion and regression of luck.

Umpire zone x walk-prone pitcher/lineup: a small zone raises totals most when a pitcher is walk-prone and lineups are patient, so umpire effects should depend on plate-discipline matchup.
Dispersion x threshold: high-total and low-total rungs price tails; park and weather affect variance as well as mean (Coors, wind games), so dispersion should depend on environment.

first_inning_and_inning_markets.label: First-inning runs and inning-level markets
first_inning_and_inning_markets.target: Whether runs are scored in a specific inning (first inning or other inning), which team outscores the other in the inning, or the inning's run total.
first_inning_and_inning_markets.mechanism: An inning is a short Markov process through base-out states with outcomes depending on the three hitters due up and the pitcher on the mound; for the first inning the top three of each lineup face the fresh starter, so the run probability (YRFI) is the union of two half-innings with probabilities driven by top-order on-base skill, handedness and starter first-trip command. Later-inning markets additionally depend on which batters are due, TTO penalty and bullpen entry, which are partly unknowable pregame. Small samples make historical first-inning splits mostly noise; PA-level simulation is preferred.

first5_markets.label: First-five-innings winner, spread and total
first5_markets.target: First-five-innings result (winner/run spread) or total runs through five innings.
first5_markets.mechanism: Through five innings runs are scored mostly against the starters (typically two trips through the order), so the market is driven by starter quality, expected exit before the fifth, the lineups' strength against the starter's hand, and the environment, with the bullpen entering only after early exits. Relative to full game, bullpen strength is de-emphasised and starter leash risk is emphasised, and ties are possible so spread and winner contracts differ by tie handling.

extras_and_delay.label: Extra innings and game delay/postponement
extras_and_delay.target: Whether the game goes to extra innings (tied after nine) or whether a delay/postponement occurs, per the contract definition.
extras_and_delay.mechanism: Extra innings are the event that the two run totals tie after nine, so probability is a function of the run distribution (higher in low-total, close games) and of late-inning scoring, with the ghost runner shaping what happens after but not the event. Delay markets are weather-timing problems: probability of precipitation or lightning near first pitch relative to roof status and umpire/team decision behaviour, mostly independent of team quality. Both are low-to-moderate probability events decided by distributional shape and exact contract wording (start delay vs in-game delay, suspended-game treatment).

season_futures.label: Division winner, season wins, postseason futures and series
season_futures.target: Team season outcomes: division title, win total thresholds, playoff/pennant/title futures, postseason series winners, records and specials.
season_futures.mechanism: Futures integrate talent estimates (projection priors updated with run differential, not record) through the remaining schedule with uncertainty, then apply tiebreakers and bracket rules; postseason series switch to a game-level dynamic program using announced starters, rest, bullpen usage and home-field pattern. Long-horizon prices depend on rating uncertainty and slow information (injuries, trades); short-horizon series prices depend on pitching availability and shortened managerial hooks. Luck regression and tiebreaker formalities matter most in close races.

Division, wildcard and win-total markets are tails of a schedule simulation with injury and rating uncertainty.

season_leaders_and_awards.label: Season leaders, player stat totals and awards
season_leaders_and_awards.target: Leader of a statistical category, a player's season total threshold, or winner of an award (MVP, Cy Young, ROY).
season_leaders_and_awards.mechanism: Season-stat and leader outcomes are current total plus rest-of-season rate times opportunity times availability, so a competitor-level simulation (with correlated team context, injury risk, and qualification rules for rate stats) gives probabilities. Awards add a voter model: production rank, team success and narrative under a specific ballot structure and timing, with finalists as information events. Early-season leaders mostly reflect luck, so regressing rates is the main lever, while late-season markets are dominated by games remaining and injuries.

Production rank x team success x ballot timing: voters weigh WAR with team outcome and cast ballots at a specific time, so late-season changes matter only before the deadline.

player_participation.label: Player participation (plays / starts / appears)
player_participation.target: Whether a named player plays or starts in a game, per the contract's definition.
player_participation.mechanism: Participation is determined by manager decisions (rest days, platoon sits), injury status and late scratches, resolved mostly when the lineup card posts; before then it is a probability from rest-day patterns, handedness of the opposing starter and injury news, afterwards it is near-certain except for in-game substitution cases. The edge is timing relative to market close and the exact definition (starts vs appears).

Lineup posting time x market close: probabilities are mixtures until the card posts, so the posting timestamp relative to close defines the information advantage.
Injury vintage x scratch risk: players listed day-to-day have elevated scratch probability late, so injury reports and warm-up news interact with lineup confirmation.

announcer_mentions.label: Broadcast word-mention markets
announcer_mentions.target: Whether a specified word or phrase is spoken in the named broadcast, per the contract's source and counting rules.
announcer_mentions.mechanism: Mention probability reflects announcer vocabulary (crew-specific base rates), the length of the broadcast and events that trigger topics (milestones, pitching changes, weather delays, named players), with the contract's definition of which feed and what counts. Baseball statistics offer little direct signal, so this is closer to a novelty/language market with sparse history; the best hypotheses concern crew habits and trigger events.

Broadcast length x word rate: delays and extra innings lengthen the broadcast, so game-length uncertainty interacts with word rate.
Wording x feed: national vs local feeds differ and the contract defines the counted feed, so crew identity interacts with rules text.

transactions.label: Transactions, coaching and personnel events
transactions.target: Whether a trade, signing, call-up, extension or manager/coach change occurs by a given date.
transactions.mechanism: Transactions follow institutional calendars and team incentives: standing (buyer vs seller), contract status, roster-rule constraints and front-office behaviour, with beat-writer reports preceding many official moves. The probability is a hazard over the contract window, estimated from reference classes and updated by reports and standings, with the resolution defined by official announcement.

offfield_markets.label: Business, non-baseball and esports novelty markets
offfield_markets.target: Events outside baseball games settled by public announcement or defined sources.
offfield_markets.mechanism: These markets are driven by organisational decisions and external events rather than on-field performance. There is little statistical structure: the best-supported hypotheses are reference-class frequencies, calendar constraints and timestamped news relative to the resolution wording. Non-baseball and esports items are not predicted by baseball inputs at all and should be treated as novelty markets with no baseball model.

player_and_team_counting_specials.label: MLB player/team counting specials (stolen bases, walks, outs recorded, earned runs, next home run)
player_and_team_counting_specials.target: A counting stat for a player or team over a game or season relative to a threshold, or which player does an event next.
player_and_team_counting_specials.mechanism: Counts are plate appearances (or batters faced) times per-PA probabilities with matchup adjustments; stolen bases add catcher and pitcher hold-time effects, walks add umpire zone and plate discipline, outs recorded depends on the starter's hook.
